title: The Hong Kong digital-asset map
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can name who regulates each digital-asset activity in Hong Kong, which regimes are live, and which are still coming.

## In 60 seconds

Hong Kong regulates digital assets activity by activity, not through one super-regulator. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) supervises banks (Authorized Institutions, AIs) and licenses stablecoin issuers; the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licenses trading platforms and sets conduct rules for securities-type activity; the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) sets policy and drafts the laws; the Legislative Council (LegCo) passes them. When a bank does securities-type virtual-asset (VA) business, it does so as an SFC Registered Institution (RI), but the HKMA is its day-to-day supervisor. Live today: the VA trading-platform regime, the Stablecoins Ordinance, the joint SFC–HKMA circulars, HKMA custody and tokenisation guidance, and the Basel cryptoasset capital standard. Coming: statutory licensing for VA dealing, custody, advisory and management, plus crypto tax reporting (CARF).

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AMLO Part 5B VA trading platform (VATP) licensing + VATP Guidelines | LegCo / SFC | 1 Jun 2023 | In force | VATPs; banks as counterparties | [S:b12bd88c7aee, p.2]; [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2] |
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) | LegCo / HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Stablecoin issuers; offerors incl. AIs | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities (Dec 2023) + supplement (Sep 2025) | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023; 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs; RIs (banks) via HKMA | [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:b79266f3da51, para 10] |
| RI circular on Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1] |
| AI interface with VAs and VASPs | HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | In force | All AIs | [S:642680fa4467, p.5] |
| Updated custody guidance (replaces Feb 2024) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs + local AI subsidiaries | [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1] |
| DLT risk-management considerations | HKMA | 16 Apr 2024 | In force | AIs (non-binding considerations) | [S:1884530ff235, p.1] |
| Basel cryptoasset standard (amendment rules + CRP-1) | HKMA / LegCo | 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:974899bbef4d, para 2]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.1] |
| VA dealing + VA custodian licensing | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks to register; HKMA frontline | [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 36]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48] |
| VA advisory + VA management licensing | FSTB + SFC | 26 May 2026 | Conclusions published | Banks may register | [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62] |

## Key facts

- The HKMA does not currently plan to stop banks taking VA exposure, provided controls and senior-management oversight are adequate. [S:642680fa4467, Prudential supervision section, p.3]
- A bank intending any VA activity should discuss it with the HKMA and get feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals, p.5]
- An AI registered by the SFC becomes an RI; the SFC keeps ultimate responsibility, while the HKMA supervises the RI day to day and the SFC may rely on that supervision. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- The joint circular reaches banks as RIs through the HKMA as frontline supervisor; intermediaries must tell the SFC ahead of time — and the HKMA too, if relevant — before beginning or changing VA-related activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- VA dealing by intermediaries may only be done by partnering with SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:8a016a912528, paras 17-18]
- The Stablecoins Ordinance commenced on 1 August 2025. [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
- The HKMA register lists two licensed stablecoin issuers, Anchorpoint Financial Limited (FRS01) and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (FRS02), both effective 10 April 2026. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- The HKMA received 36 first-batch stablecoin applications and says the number of licences will stay very limited. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply para 1 and (2)]
- The SFC's live list showed 13 licensed VATPs at its 29 May 2026 update; being on the applicant list is not the same as being licensed. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table; applicant section]
- The HKMA's 2026 custody annex expects at least 98% of client VAs in cold storage and seed/key generation, storage and backup in Hong Kong. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), para 11(l) and fn 8]
- The Basel cryptoasset capital, disclosure and exposure-limit rules took effect on 1 January 2026. [S:974899bbef4d, para 2]
- Under CRP-1, a bank must notify the HKMA before acquiring a new type of cryptoasset and treat it as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees otherwise. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- For the coming VA dealing and custody regimes, the SFC will license and set standards, and the HKMA will be frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- Banks must register with the SFC, in consultation with the HKMA, to deal in VAs under the proposed dealing regime. [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 1.10]
- No grandfathering will apply when the VA dealing and custody regimes commence; firms already vetted get an expedited track. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]
- The CARF bill was gazetted on 22 May 2026 and had its First Reading on 3 June 2026; CARF duties are set to start on 1 January 2027. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]
- The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) will run CARF registration through a future portal; the Insurance Authority (IA) appears in this corpus only as a co-backer of FiNETech and a contributor to the HKMA's DLT study. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Reporting portal section]; [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 5]; [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Discuss any planned VA activity with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- [ ] As an RI, give advance notice to the SFC and HKMA before starting or changing VA dealing, advice or asset management, including a change of client type. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- [ ] Treat cryptoasset exposures under the Banking (Capital) Rules Part 12 and CRP-1 from 1 January 2026. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 1.4.1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Set prudent VA exposure limits and conservative loan-to-value ratios for VA collateral. [S:642680fa4467, p.3]
- [ ] Keep client digital assets segregated from the bank's own assets. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 6]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Notify the HKMA before acquiring any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- [ ] Discuss custody plans with the HKMA before offering custody. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] For VA dealing, route business only through SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- [ ] Check a VATP's status on the SFC's licensed list, not the applicant list. [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section]
- [ ] Check a stablecoin issuer against the HKMA register. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 5]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The bank's VA conduct duties reach it as an RI supervised by the HKMA, not through direct SFC supervision. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline, not the SFC's, is the bank's primary AML text; RIs only need to have regard to SFC Chapter 12. [S:7bfdad704174, Ch.1 fn 1]

**To business heads**
- Any new VA product needs an HKMA discussion before launch, and RIs must pre-notify the SFC and HKMA. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]; [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- Only two stablecoin issuers are licensed; the HKMA says licences will stay very limited. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)]

**To the CEO**
- The government plans a single SFC-led licensing model for VA dealing and custody, with the HKMA as the banks' frontline regulator. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- No grandfathering is planned when these regimes start. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]

**To Risk / CRO**
- The Basel cryptoasset standard applies from 1 January 2026; unassessed exposures sit in Group 2b by default. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.4.1-1.4.2]
- Custody requires at least 98% of client VAs in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l)]

## Common mix-ups

- "The SFC supervises our VA business directly." No: the SFC holds ultimate responsibility, but the HKMA is the RI's day-to-day supervisor. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- "The 50%/100% insurance rule applies to our custody." The fixed 50% cold / 100% hot cover belongs to the SFC VATP regime; the HKMA's 2026 annex instead makes the bank liable for losses attributable to it and requires adequate financial resources. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22]; [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- "A deemed or applicant VATP is licensed." Not so; only the licensed list shows licensed platforms. [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section]
- "The 2022 joint circular still applies." The December 2023 joint circular superseded the January 2022 and October 2023 versions. [S:8a016a912528, note after para 3, p.1]
- "The dealing and custody bills are law." They are at consultation-conclusions stage; the government targets a 2026 bill. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]

## Read these first

1. **Regulatory approaches to AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs** — HKMA, 28 Jan 2022. Read pp.3-5 (prudential, AML, investor protection, prior discussion). The HKMA's base position on banks and VAs. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20220128-1-EN
2. **SPM SB-1 Supervision of Regulated Activities of SFC-Registered AIs (V.4)** — HKMA, 12 Sep 2025. Read paras 2.1.3, 2.2.4, 4.16.1 and 5.6. Explains why the HKMA, not the SFC, supervises your RI business day to day. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250909-3-EN/SB-1.PDF
3. **Policy Statement 2.0 on the Development of Digital Assets in Hong Kong** — FSTB, 26 Jun 2025. Read paras 4-6 and 16. Sets the LEAP framework and the SFC-lead/HKMA-frontline split for new regimes. https://gia.info.gov.hk/general/202506/26/P2025062600269_500089_1_1750909574183.pdf

## Open items

- The VA dealing/custodian/advisory/management bill: FSTB said in June 2026 it would be introduced within 2026; no bill text or gazettal is in the corpus as of 25 Sep 2026. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- CARF bill: First Reading done on 3 June 2026; the corpus has no record of passage. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2]
- No Insurance Authority rulebook on digital assets is in the corpus; insurer-side rules are a gap.
- The VATP list is live; the 13-platform count is a 29 May 2026 snapshot. [S:b14be2203d39, Footer]

title: How Hong Kong rules are made and how to read them
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can place any document on the law-making path, tell how binding it is, and cite it to the paragraph.

## In 60 seconds

Most Hong Kong digital-asset rules follow the same path: a consultation paper, published conclusions, a bill gazetted and passed by the Legislative Council (LegCo), a commencement notice, then a transition period. Below the statute sit the regulator's own instruments: rules (subsidiary legislation), Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) modules, guidelines, circulars, codes and FAQs. Their force differs, so check each document's own *classification* or *application* note. For a bank, the key reading rule is in the HKMA's anti-money-laundering (AML) Guideline: both *must* and *should* are mandatory. Most HKMA documents live in the Banking Regulatory Document Repository (BRDR); SFC circulars live on its e-Distribution site; FSTB papers and government press releases carry the legislative milestones.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026. Worked examples of each stage.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stablecoin issuer regime: consultation paper, then conclusions (Jul 2024) | FSTB + HKMA | 27 Dec 2023 | Superseded | Prospective issuers | [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1]; [S:92481c3c89ce, para 29] |
| Stablecoins Bill gazetted; First Reading 18 Dec 2024 | Government / LegCo | 6 Dec 2024 | Superseded | Issuers | [S:a9a82f2b38ce, paras 1, 5] |
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) commencement | SFST notice | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Issuers, offerors | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| Banking (Capital/Disclosure/Exposure Limits) Amendment Rules 2025 | HKMA / LegCo | Gazetted 11 Jul 2025; effective 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:974899bbef4d, paras 1-2] |
| CRP-1 clarification letter on para 2.6.4 | HKMA | 3 Jun 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1] |
| VA dealing and custodian regimes | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks (registration), LCs, VATPs | [S:6186c01c6649, p.3]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48] |
| VA advisory and management regimes | FSTB + SFC | 26 May 2026 | Conclusions published | Banks, LCs | [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62] |
| CARF / amended CRS bill | FSTB / LegCo | Gazetted 22 May 2026 | Bill before LegCo | Crypto-asset service providers | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |

## Key facts

- The legislative path is visible in the stablecoin regime: consultation conclusions in July 2024 said a bill would follow by end-2024. [S:92481c3c89ce, para 29]
- The Stablecoins Bill was gazetted on 6 December 2024 and read a first time in LegCo on 18 December 2024. [S:a9a82f2b38ce, paras 1, 5]
- LegCo passed the bill on 21 May 2025; the Ordinance provides a six-month non-contravention period. [S:35e1ac2b815a, paras 1, 3]
- A separate gazetted notice set 1 August 2025 as commencement, and the notices went to LegCo for negative vetting. [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1-3]
- Subsidiary legislation such as the Banking (Capital) Amendment Rules 2025 goes through a 28-day LegCo negative-vetting period; for the cryptoasset rules it expired without extension. [S:974899bbef4d, para 1]
- AMLO amendments passed on 7 December 2022 did not take effect until 1 June 2023, giving industry time to prepare. [S:b12bd88c7aee, p.2]
- Transitions can be hard stops: pre-existing VATPs had a 12-month non-contravention window to 31 May 2024, and the SFC could not extend the 29 February 2024 deeming deadline. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 20]
- For the coming VA dealing and custody regimes, no deeming or grandfathering will be given. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48]
- The HKMA AML Guideline is issued under AMLO s.7 and Banking Ordinance s.7(3), and compliance is enforced through both ordinances. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.1, 1.3]
- In that Guideline, both *must* and *should* denote a mandatory requirement. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- SPM modules state their own force: SB-1 is a statutory guideline under Banking Ordinance s.7(3), while CRP-1 is a non-statutory guidance note. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, cover, Classification]
- Where CRP-1 and the Banking (Capital) Rules differ, the Rules prevail. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- Some HKMA papers say they are non-binding: the April 2024 DLT considerations are non-binding, non-exhaustive and discussed bilaterally. [S:1884530ff235, Annex introduction, p.1]
- A circular can change a module at once: the 3 June 2026 letter loosened CRP-1 para 2.6.4 with immediate effect, pending a later text update. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4]
- SFC VATP Guidelines are published under SFO s.399 and AMLO s.53ZTK. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1 note]
- Later circulars can supersede earlier ones outright: the Dec 2023 joint circular replaced the Jan 2022 and Oct 2023 versions. [S:8a016a912528, note after para 3, p.1]
- The HKMA's 2026 custody letter supersedes the February 2024 custody circular. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- Policy speeches are not rules: the 2026-27 Budget states intentions that need later bills or regulatory issuances. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Read *should* in the HKMA AML Guideline as mandatory, not optional. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- [ ] Apply the Banking (Capital) Rules Part 12 where they differ from CRP-1. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- [ ] Update CRP-1 classification practice for the 3 June 2026 clarification of para 2.6.4. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep a regulatory inventory that records each document's classification and supersession, e.g. 2024 custody circular replaced by the 2026 letter. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- [ ] Track commencement dates separately from passage dates (e.g. AMLO: passed Dec 2022, effective 1 June 2023). [S:b12bd88c7aee, p.2]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Engage the SFC or HKMA early on pre-application for the coming dealing regime; firms that do not may have to stop on commencement. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 33-34]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Distinguish a VATP's licensed status from deemed or applicant status. [S:c787f990209d, 'Reminder for investors']

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Our AML Guideline treats *should* as a requirement; there is no soft reading. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- Check each SPM module's classification: SB-1 is statutory, CRP-1 is a guidance note beneath the Capital Rules. [S:8934af8cc884, cover]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]

**To business heads**
- Conclusions papers are not law yet; the dealing and custody regimes still need a bill. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]
- When the new regimes start there is no grandfathering, so early SFC/HKMA engagement matters. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 33-34]

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong's path is consultation, conclusions, bill, commencement and transition; the Stablecoins Ordinance took about 19 months from consultation to commencement. [S:92481c3c89ce, para 29]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
- Budget and Policy Address items are stated intentions, not obligations. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104-109]

**To Risk / CRO**
- The cryptoasset capital rules passed negative vetting and apply from 1 January 2026. [S:974899bbef4d, paras 1-2]
- HKMA letters can amend capital guidance with immediate effect, as in June 2026. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]

## Common mix-ups

- "Should in HKMA guidance is best practice." In the AML Guideline it is mandatory. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- "All SPM modules have the same force." SB-1 is statutory; CRP-1 is non-statutory and yields to the Rules. [S:8934af8cc884, cover]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- "The June 2026 CRP-1 letter tightened Group 1 tests." It widened how para 2.6.4 can be met. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- "Passage means in force." AMLO amendments passed in December 2022 took effect in June 2023. [S:b12bd88c7aee, p.2]
- "Existing players will be grandfathered into new VA regimes." The conclusions say no deeming arrangement. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]

## Read these first

1. **Guideline on AML/CFT (For Authorized Institutions), revised May 2023** — HKMA, 25 May 2023. Read Chapter 1, paras 1.1-1.8 and footnote 1. Defines how binding the text is and who it binds. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20230525-4-EN/AML-2.pdf
2. **SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets** — HKMA, 27 Nov 2025 (V.1, effective 1 Jan 2026). Read the cover page and paras 1.1.4, 1.4.1-1.4.2. Shows how a guidance note sits under statutory rules. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20251125-15-EN
3. **Rules on cryptoassets standard and other updates** — HKMA, 15 Aug 2025. Read paras 1-2. A one-page view of negative vetting and commencement. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20250815-1-EN

**How to use paragraph references.** Cite HKMA SPM modules and guidelines by paragraph (e.g. CRP-1 para 2.1.2). HKMA circulars often have no numbered paragraphs, so cite heading plus page (e.g. Implementation, p.2). SFC circulars number paragraphs (e.g. joint circular para 31). BRDR landing pages (brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/…) link the PDF and related documents; SFC circulars open from apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb by reference number (e.g. 23EC66). [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]

## Open items

- No FAQ, code of practice or SFC Code of Conduct text on how SFO s.399 guidelines are weighed in proceedings is in the corpus; this module does not state their legal effect beyond what the documents say.
- The CRP-1 text itself had not been updated for the June 2026 clarification as of the letter. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, para 4]
- Commencement dates for the VA dealing, custody, advisory and management regimes are not yet set. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- CARF bill passage is not recorded in the corpus. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2]

title: Where policy is heading
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can say what the government, the SFC and the HKMA have officially said they will do next, and by when, using only their own words and dates.

## In 60 seconds

Hong Kong's digital-asset direction is set out in a short stack of official strategy papers. The FSTB's 2022 Policy Statement set out its founding regulatory principle (quoted in Key facts below); its 2025 Policy Statement 2.0 added the LEAP framework and made the SFC the lead licensing authority, with the HKMA as frontline regulator for banks. The SFC's ASPIRe roadmap (Feb 2025) lists 12 initiatives, most of them still exploratory. The HKMA moved from Fintech 2025 to Fintech 2030, then published a Fintech Promotion Blueprint (Feb 2026) and asked bank boards to endorse a business-model plan. The 16 Sep 2026 Policy Address and the 2026-27 Budget add dated targets: tokenised Exchange Fund Bills, EnsembleTX settlement upgrades, and a VA licensing bill in 2026. All of these are statements of intent until a law or rule gives them force.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Policy Statement on Development of VA in Hong Kong | FSTB | 31 Oct 2022 | Superseded | Market-wide (PS 2.0 is the next phase) | [S:f587b828e3fa, para 4]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 3] |
| Fintech 2025 | HKMA | 8 Jun 2021 | Superseded | Banks (succeeded by Fintech 2030) | [S:f8eed6b2e069, p.1]; [S:1131a8814d96, para 3] |
| ASPIRe roadmap | SFC | 19 Feb 2025 | Exploratory | VATPs, LCs, RIs (only custody timeline dated) | [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1] |
| Policy Statement 2.0 (LEAP) | FSTB | 26 Jun 2025 | Stated target | Market-wide; banks via HKMA | [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] |
| Fintech 2030 (DART) | HKMA | 3 Nov 2025 | Stated target | Banks | [S:1131a8814d96, para 3] |
| Fintech Promotion Blueprint | HKMA | 3 Feb 2026 | Stated target | Banks, fintech providers | [S:b0607b779270, paras 2-8] |
| Strategic Review of Business Models circular | HKMA | 9 Mar 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2] |
| 2026-27 Budget | Financial Secretary | 25 Feb 2026 | Stated target | Market-wide | [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104-114] |
| Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address | Chief Executive | 16 Sep 2026 | Stated target | Market-wide | [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35, 49-51] |

## Key facts

- The 2022 Policy Statement committed the government to "same activity, same risks, same regulation" and to a mandatory VA service-provider licensing regime. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 4, 6]
- It also flagged stablecoins as a priority and named three pilots: NFT issuance, a tokenised government green bond, and e-HKD. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 9-11]
- Policy Statement 2.0 replaced the government's use of *virtual assets* with *digital assets*; the legal term under AMLO remains *virtual asset*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1]
- LEAP stands for Legal and regulatory streamlining, Expanding tokenised products, Advancing use cases, and People and partnership development. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 4]
- Under PS 2.0 the SFC leads licensing for digital-asset dealing and custody, while the HKMA is frontline regulator for banks' dealing and custodian activities. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- PS 2.0 also said the government would extend fund tax concessions to specified digital assets from year of assessment 2025/26, subject to LegCo approval. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]
- ASPIRe has five pillars (Access, Safeguards, Products, Infrastructure, Relationships) and 12 initiatives; custodian licensing preparation was targeted for end-2025. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1]
- ASPIRe says the SFC will explore moving from a fixed cold-storage ratio to outcome-based custody standards. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]
- Fintech 2030 has four pillars (Data and payments, AI, Resilience, Tokenisation) and over 40 initiatives, including tokenised government bonds and the Ensemble pilot. [S:1131a8814d96, para 3 and 'Tokenisation of Finance']
- The Fintech Promotion Blueprint announced four flagship projects, including a Quantum Preparedness Index and a Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline for AI/DLT providers. [S:b0607b779270, paras 5, 7]
- The HKMA expects each AI's board to oversee and endorse a strategic business plan within six months of 9 March 2026, covering DLT and other technology change. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
- The 2025 Policy Address committed to introducing a bill in 2026 for licensing digital-asset dealing and custodian providers. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex item 22]
- The 2026-27 Budget repeated the 2026 bill target and said a CARF amendment bill would come in the first half of 2026, with implementation over two years. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108]
- The Budget also said CMU OmniClear would launch a digital asset platform in 2026 for digital bond issuance and settlement. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]
- The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA will test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by year-end, covering more than $1.3 trillion of bills. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- The HKMA aims to have central bank digital currency settlement running around the clock through EnsembleTX by roughly end-2026, with more tokenised-deposit use cases to follow. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- The SFC will enhance VA licensing regimes, let licensed platforms trade regulated stablecoins, and switch on a system for monitoring digital-asset custody from mid-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49(i), 49(iii), 51(iii)]
- Customs and Excise plans a digital-asset transaction analytics system by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Part II item 209]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Have the board oversee and endorse a formal strategic business plan addressing DLT and related technology within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Track the 2026 bill target for VA dealing and custody licensing, since banks will need SFC registration with the HKMA as frontline regulator. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- [ ] Track CARF start dates (1 Jan 2027 for CARF, 1 Jan 2028 for amended CRS) in the bill. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Discuss any new digital-asset activity with the HKMA before launch, as the March 2026 circular restates. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
- [ ] Be ready to submit the business plan via the HKMA Survey Tool if invited. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] No counterparty duties arise from policy statements themselves; apply the rules in B2 and B3.

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Policy statements, Budgets and Policy Addresses create no obligations; the business-model circular does create a board expectation. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]; [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2]
- Government now says *digital assets*, but AMLO still defines *virtual asset*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1]

**To business heads**
- The SFC plans to let licensed platforms trade regulated stablecoins and use them to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- EnsembleTX is to add 24/7 CBDC settlement by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA wants banks to act as trusted intermediaries between traditional finance and digital assets, and expects a board-endorsed plan. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.1-2]
- The government's stated 2026 target is one bill for VA dealing and custody licensing. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex item 22]

**To Risk / CRO**
- The Blueprint's Quantum Preparedness Index will measure post-quantum readiness; the HKMA's first score was 2.3 out of 10. [S:b0607b779270, para 5]; [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]
- ASPIRe may shift custody rules toward outcome-based standards, but that is still exploratory. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]

## Common mix-ups

- "Policy Statement 2.0 changed the law." It sets directions; tax concessions, for example, need LegCo approval. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]
- "ASPIRe items are rules." Most initiatives are framed as things the SFC will explore or consider. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]
- "The first stablecoin licences came in March 2026 as the Budget said." The Budget said next month; the HKMA granted them on 10 April 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 105]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 1]
- "The business-model circular is about crypto only." It covers DLT, agentic AI and cloud, with a reminder on digital-asset pre-launch discussion. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.1-2]

## Read these first

1. **Policy Statement 2.0 on the Development of Digital Assets in Hong Kong** — FSTB, 26 Jun 2025. Read paras 3-6, 9-11, 15-16. The current government framework (LEAP) and regulator roles. https://gia.info.gov.hk/general/202506/26/P2025062600269_500089_1_1750909574183.pdf
2. **Strategic Review of Business Models amid Digital Transformation** — HKMA, 9 Mar 2026. Read the whole two pages. The one policy document here that asks something of your board. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260309-1-EN/20260309-1-EN.pdf
3. **The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address** — 16 Sep 2026. Read paras 35, 49-51 and 99 (pp.23, 27, 34). The latest dated targets for HKMA, SFC and CMU OmniClear. https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

## Open items

- The 2026 VA licensing bill had not appeared in the corpus by 25 Sep 2026, though the government said it would come later in 2026. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- The Blueprint's Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline and Quantum Preparedness Index detail documents are not in the corpus.
- The 2023 Policy Address contains no virtual-asset content. [S:61458655f37b, paras 41, 72(iv)]
- Canon locator correction: the 2026 Policy Address digital-bond items are in para 35(ii)-(iv) on p.23, not para 34 as one canon entry states; this module uses the text.

For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain which legal hat the bank wears for each digital-asset activity, who supervises it, and which rulebook binds which entity in the group.

## In 60 seconds

A bank in Hong Kong is an Authorized Institution (AI) under the Banking Ordinance, supervised by the HKMA. When it carries on SFC-regulated activities such as dealing in or advising on securities, it registers with the SFC and becomes a Registered Institution (RI); the HKMA stays its day-to-day supervisor under SPM module SB-1. A group subsidiary licensed by the SFC is a Licensed Corporation (LC) and is supervised by the SFC directly. The joint SFC–HKMA virtual-asset (VA) circulars reach the bank in its RI capacity, through the HKMA. Under the coming VA dealing and custody regimes, banks will register with the SFC while the HKMA remains their frontline regulator; bank subsidiaries doing VA custody will be SFC-regulated. Some HKMA circulars bind all AIs, others only RIs, so scope checks matter.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPM SB-1 (V.4) Supervision of SFC-registered AIs | HKMA | 12 Sep 2025 | In force | RIs | [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Application] |
| AML/CFT Guideline (For AIs) | HKMA | 25 May 2023 | In force | All AIs incl. RIs | [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3] |
| Joint circular on VA-related activities + supplement | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023; 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs; RIs | [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:b79266f3da51, para 4] |
| RI circular: Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs only | [S:a0bd48559762, footnote 3, p.2] |
| AI letter: Relevant Stablecoin-related activities | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| RI circular: VA financing, shared order book, withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs only | [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2] |
| Custody guidance (updated) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs + subsidiaries of local AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2] |
| VA dealing regime (banks register; HKMA frontline) | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks, SVFs, LCs, VATPs | [S:f673ef6dcb63, paras 1.10, 2.36]; [S:6186c01c6649, para 36] |
| VA custodian regime | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks, bank subsidiaries, custodians | [S:30b60438f017, paras 2.12(a), 2.48]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 41] |
| VA advisory and management regimes | FSTB + SFC | 26 May 2026 | Conclusions published | Banks may register | [S:6186c01c6649, footnotes 9-10] |

## Key facts

- An AI that carries on regulated activities must register with the SFC as an RI under SFO s.119. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2, 2.2.1]
- The SFC holds ultimate responsibility, but the HKMA is the RI's front-line supervisor, and the SFC may rely on HKMA supervision under SFO s.5(3). [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- Each RI appoints at least two executive officers per regulated activity, each needing the Monetary Authority's prior written consent; one must always be available. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.4]
- Every relevant individual performing a regulated function must be on the HKMA Register before starting. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 4.3.1, 4.3.5]
- An associated entity of an RI is a company in a controlling-entity relationship with it that receives or holds the RI's client assets in Hong Kong. [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1]
- An RI should notify the SFC and HKMA if it intends to engage in any VA activity or change it, including the client type. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- The HKMA AML Guideline binds all AIs, including RIs; RIs and AI associated entities must also have regard to the SFC AML guideline, including its Chapter 12 on VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 and footnote 1]
- The joint circular addresses intermediaries, meaning LCs and RIs; it requires advance notice to the SFC and, where applicable, the HKMA. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- The Sep 2025 supplement lets LCs and RIs offer staking through segregated accounts with an SFC-licensed platform or an AI. [S:b79266f3da51, paras 4-5]
- The May 2026 Relevant Stablecoin relief applies to RIs only; it does not reach AIs that are not RIs or an issuer's dealings in its own coin. [S:a0bd48559762, footnote 3, p.2]
- A separate HKMA letter asks all AIs doing Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice or portfolio management to meet the RI standards and to discuss with the HKMA first. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1; Implementation, p.2]
- Under the Stablecoins Ordinance, only specified licensed institutions may offer a fiat-referenced stablecoin in Hong Kong. [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 3]
- A bank can itself be a licensed issuer: HSBC holds licence FRS02. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- For an issuer that is an AI, the one-third independent-director expectation does not apply; the Banking Ordinance governs instead. [S:240be6833157, para 7.1.3]
- Under the proposed VA dealing regime, banks must register with the SFC, in consultation with the HKMA. [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 1.10]
- The HKMA would be frontline regulator for banks' VA dealing, with powers to inspect premises and investigate. [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 2.36]
- For VA custody, the HKMA would be frontline regulator for banks, but VA custodians that are subsidiaries of locally incorporated banks would be regulated by the SFC. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]
- Banks doing VA custody would rely on existing HKMA capital requirements instead of the HK$10m/HK$3m custodian baseline. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41-42]
- Only banks may register (rather than be licensed) for VA advisory or VA management services. [S:6186c01c6649, footnotes 9-10]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Hold SFC registration for each regulated activity carried on, with at least two HKMA-consented executive officers per activity. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.1, 2.2.4]
- [ ] Register relevant individuals on the HKMA Register before they start. [S:8934af8cc884, para 4.3.1]
- [ ] Apply the HKMA AML Guideline bank-wide; for RI and associated-entity business, also have regard to SFC AML Chapter 12. [S:7bfdad704174, footnote 1]
- [ ] Make sure subsidiaries of the locally incorporated bank that do custody or staking comply with HKMA standards. [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]; [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Map every digital-asset activity to its entity and capacity (AI, RI, LC subsidiary, associated entity) before applying a circular. [S:a0bd48559762, footnote 3, p.2]
- [ ] Keep the relevant-individual database current and notify changes within 7 business days. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 4.3.6, 5.5]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Notify the SFC and HKMA before starting or changing VA activities. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- [ ] Notify the HKMA in advance of an intended SFC registration application. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.3]
- [ ] Engage the SFC or HKMA early on pre-application for the coming dealing regime. [S:6186c01c6649, para 33]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Confirm a stablecoin issuer counterparty is on the HKMA register. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register note]
- [ ] Confirm VA dealing partners are SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Our VA conduct rules reach us as an RI; the HKMA supervises, the SFC keeps ultimate responsibility. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- Scope matters: some May 2026 relief applies only to RIs, while the stablecoin-activity letter covers all AIs. [S:a0bd48559762, fn 3]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]

**To business heads**
- New VA services need advance notice to the SFC and HKMA through our RI registration. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- A custody subsidiary would be SFC-regulated under the coming custodian regime, not HKMA-supervised as the bank is. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]

**To the CEO**
- Under the coming regimes, the bank registers with the SFC while the HKMA stays frontline regulator. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- Executive officers can lose HKMA consent for misconduct, which could affect the RI's ability to operate. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 6.3, 6.7]

**To Risk / CRO**
- A bank VA custodian would use existing HKMA capital rules, not the custodian capital baseline. [S:f41a543388bc, para 41]
- VA-only secured loans count as clean loans for capital purposes. [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5]

## Common mix-ups

- "SFC AML Chapter 12 binds the whole bank." It applies to RIs and AI associated entities on a have-regard basis only. [S:7bfdad704174, footnote 1]
- "The joint circular is an SFC rule aimed at brokers, not us." It addresses RIs too, and reaches banks through HKMA frontline supervision. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- "All AIs get the May 2026 stablecoin relief." That circular covers RIs only. [S:a0bd48559762, footnote 3, p.2]
- "A bank subsidiary custodian is supervised like the bank." It would be regulated by the SFC. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]
- "VA financing rules apply to every AI." The May 2026 financing circular applies to RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1-2]

## Read these first

1. **SPM SB-1 Supervision of Regulated Activities of SFC-Registered AIs (V.4)** — HKMA, 12 Sep 2025. Read paras 1.1.1, 2.1-2.2, 4.3, 4.16.1, 5.6. The rulebook for your RI status. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250909-3-EN/SB-1.PDF
2. **Public Consultation on Legislative Proposal to Regulate Dealing in Virtual Assets** — FSTB/SFC, 27 Jun 2025. Read paras 1.10 and 2.36. How banks will be registered and supervised. https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/VADEALING_consultation_paper_en.pdf
3. **Virtual asset-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins** — HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read footnote 3 (p.2), paras (1)-(4) and Implementation (p.9). A worked example of RI-only scope. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The bill for VA dealing, custody, advisory and management has not been published; final bank registration mechanics are not yet in statute. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- The corpus has no HKMA or SFC text on how the new AMLO registrations will interact with existing SFO registration for an RI beyond expedited processing. [S:6186c01c6649, para 36]
- The corpus lacks the Banking Ordinance and SFO text on executive officers; SB-1 is the only source used.

For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can list every talk-to-the-regulator-first duty that applies to a bank's digital-asset plans, and explain the HKMA's engagement channels: the Supervisory Incubator, the stablecoin issuer sandbox and the 2026 business-model review.

## In 60 seconds

Since January 2022 the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has asked one thing of every bank before a virtual-asset (VA) launch: discuss the plan with the HKMA and get its feedback on your risk controls. Later circulars repeat that step for tokenised products, custody, staking and services in HKMA-licensed (Relevant) stablecoins. When the bank acts as a Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) Registered Institution (RI), it must also give advance notice to both the SFC and the HKMA before starting or changing VA dealing, advice or asset management. The capital rules add a separate trigger: notify the HKMA before acquiring a new type of cryptoasset. For distributed ledger technology (DLT) projects, the HKMA runs a Supervisory Incubator with a dedicated team and optional live trials. In March 2026 the HKMA asked every bank's board to endorse a digital-transformation business plan within six months.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIs' interface with VAs and VA service providers (VASPs) | HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | In force | All Authorized Institutions (AIs) | [S:642680fa4467, p.5] |
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 | In force | Licensed corporations (LCs); RIs via HKMA | [S:8a016a912528, para 31] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6] |
| Custody circular (first version) | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | Superseded | AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] |
| Updated custody guidance and Annex | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] |
| Staking from custodial services | HKMA | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3, Implementation] |
| Supervisory Incubator for DLT | HKMA | 8 Jan 2025 | Pilot | AIs | [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] |
| SPM SB-1 (V.4) | HKMA | 12 Sep 2025 | In force | RIs | [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6] |
| Supplemental joint circular | SFC + HKMA | 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs; RIs | [S:b79266f3da51, para 10] |
| SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets | HKMA | 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] |
| SPM CR-L-5 Major Acquisitions (V.3) | HKMA | 27 Nov 2025 | In force | Locally incorporated AIs | [S:13365a31e794, para 1.1 and fn 1] |
| Strategic Review of Business Models | HKMA | 9 Mar 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4] |
| RI circular and AI letter on Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs; all AIs | [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2] |
| SFC circular 26EC26 on Relevant Stablecoin services | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | VA trading platforms (VATPs); LCs | [S:19d52ade6849, para 12] |

## Key facts

- A bank planning any VA activity should discuss it with the HKMA (and other regulators where relevant) and obtain feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals section, p.5]
- Before selling or issuing tokenised products, a bank should have policies and controls in place and discuss its plans with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6]
- A bank, or a local bank's subsidiary, that intends to offer digital-asset custody should discuss it with the HKMA first and show, to the HKMA's satisfaction, that it meets the Annex standards. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- The February 2024 circular asked existing custodians to confirm compliance to the HKMA within six months; the May 2026 letter supersedes it and simply asks existing custodians to review and revise their controls. [S:6bccca749ac2, Implementation, p.2]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- Before launching staking from custody, a bank should have adequate policies and controls and discuss its plans with the HKMA in advance. [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3, Implementation]
- Intermediaries, including RIs, should give the SFC, and where relevant the HKMA, advance notice before starting VA activities or changing them, including a change in client type. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- The September 2025 supplement lists changes needing prior notice: client type; first VA deposits or withdrawals; first staking service; first subscriptions or redemptions paid in VAs; other material changes. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]
- SB-1 expects an RI to tell the SFC and the HKMA when it plans to start, or change, VA activities. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- An RI needs at least two executive officers per regulated activity, and each appointment needs the HKMA's prior written consent. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 4.3.9]
- RIs should give the HKMA and SFC advance notice before distributing, dealing in, advising on or managing Relevant Stablecoins, or materially changing those arrangements. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- All AIs (not only RIs) should discuss Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice or portfolio management with the HKMA before starting. [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2]
- Under CRP-1, a bank must notify the HKMA before acquiring a new type of cryptoasset and treat it as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees a better classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- A locally incorporated AI needs the Monetary Authority's written consent to acquire shares worth 5% or more of its Tier 1 capital; equity-like cryptoassets count as shares. [S:13365a31e794, para 1.1 and fn 1]
- The Supervisory Incubator, launched on 8 January 2025, gives banks one supervisory contact point to confirm DLT risk controls before full launch, with optional live trials; tokenised deposits were an initial focus. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]
- Incubator participants may get some supervisory flexibility, decided case by case. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and fn 2]
- The HKMA expects each bank's board to oversee and endorse a formal strategic business plan on these technology shifts within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- That circular repeats that new digital-asset activities should be discussed with the HKMA before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]
- The stablecoin issuer sandbox (March 2024) let would-be issuers test in a limited way; admission was not a licence or an endorsement. [S:28616d929735, paras 8-9]
- The HKMA later said sandbox participation is neither a precondition for nor a guarantee of a licence. [S:e0b249a7eb8c, Licensing regime section, para 5]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Discuss each new VA product or service with the HKMA and obtain its feedback on risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- [ ] Have the board oversee and endorse the strategic business plan the March 2026 circular asks for. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- [ ] Get HKMA prior written consent for each RI executive officer. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.4]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Track the changes that trigger prior notice: client type, first VA deposits or withdrawals, first staking, first VA-funded subscriptions, other material changes. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]
- [ ] If the bank already offers custody, review and revise controls against the 2026 Annex. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- [ ] Hold any reclassified cryptoasset in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees an upgrade. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.1.3-2.1.5]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Tokenised products, custody, staking: discuss with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.6]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]; [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3]
- [ ] RI VA activities and changes: notify the SFC and the HKMA in advance. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]; [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- [ ] Relevant Stablecoin activities: RIs notify the HKMA and SFC; all AIs discuss with the HKMA. [S:a0bd48559762, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.2]
- [ ] New cryptoasset type: notify the HKMA before acquisition. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- [ ] Equity-like token stakes at or above 5% of Tier 1: seek consent; other significant acquisitions: give at least one month's notice. [S:13365a31e794, paras 1.1, 2.9.1]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Do not treat a firm's sandbox status as a licence; check the register instead. [S:28616d929735, para 9]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 5]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Every VA, tokenisation, custody, staking or stablecoin launch starts with an HKMA discussion; RI activities also need advance notice to the SFC and HKMA. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]; [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- The 2026 custody letter dropped the six-month confirmation; existing custodians must review and revise instead. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]

**To business heads**
- The HKMA discussion comes before go-live for any new digital-asset activity, as the March 2026 circular restates. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]
- Changing client type, or first allowing VA deposits, staking or VA-funded subscriptions, needs prior notice. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA asked each board to endorse a digital-transformation business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- The Supervisory Incubator lets us test DLT ideas with a dedicated HKMA team before full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]

**To Risk / CRO**
- A new cryptoasset type needs HKMA notice first and sits in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees otherwise. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- Equity-like tokens count as shares for the 5%-of-Tier-1 consent test. [S:13365a31e794, fn 1]

## Common mix-ups

- "Telling the SFC is enough." SB-1 expects RIs to tell both regulators, and the HKMA's own circulars add a prior-discussion step. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]; [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- "The SFC's 26EC26 notice rule on admitting stablecoins binds us." It is addressed to VATPs and LCs; for RIs the HKMA's RI circular sets the advance-notice duty. [S:19d52ade6849, para 12]; [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- "Every crypto trade needs a CRP-1 notification." Only a new type does: a first Bitcoin position triggers it, but Bitcoin futures after existing spot exposure do not. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2 and fn 7]
- "The six-month custody confirmation still applies." It belonged to the superseded 2024 circular. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- "Incubator or sandbox entry means approval." Incubator flexibility is case by case; sandbox admission was not an endorsement. [S:fae36c380174, p.1]; [S:28616d929735, para 9]

## Read these first

1. **Regulatory approaches to AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs**, HKMA, 28 Jan 2022. Read pp.3-5, ending with the AIs' VA-related proposals section. It is the root of the prior-discussion expectation. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20220128-1-EN
2. **SPM SB-1 Supervision of Regulated Activities of SFC-Registered AIs (V.4)**, HKMA, 12 Sep 2025. Read paras 2.1.3, 2.2.4, 4.3 and 5.6. Sets RI notification and executive-officer consent duties. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250909-3-EN/SB-1.PDF
3. **VA-related activities in relation to Relevant Stablecoins (RI circular)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read Background (pp.1-2) and Implementation (p.9). The newest advance-notice duty. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- No HKMA form, template or response timeline for prior discussion appears in the corpus.
- The six-month window in the March 2026 business-model circular ran to about 9 September 2026; the corpus has no HKMA follow-up on submissions. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- The corpus has no public list of Supervisory Incubator participants.
- Once the VA dealing and custody bills are enacted, banks will need SFC registration in consultation with the HKMA; no bill text is in the corpus yet (see A1).

title: Governance, risk and technology expectations
partTitle: Your bank as a regulated entity
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain what the HKMA expects of the board, of new-product risk assessment, of DLT and vendor risk, and of private-key control, and point to the paragraph for each.

## In 60 seconds

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) puts digital-asset risk on the board's desk. Its Pillar 2 guideline says the board and senior management should understand the risks of new or complex activities, and names cryptoasset activities as an example. Before any new product or new technology goes live, the bank's anti-money laundering (AML) guideline requires a money laundering and terrorist financing (ML/TF) risk assessment. For distributed ledger technology (DLT), the HKMA published ten non-binding risk considerations in April 2024 and a longer research study in March 2025. Custody, staking and tokenised-product circulars add concrete vendor due-diligence and key-management expectations: keys in tamper-resistant hardware, generated and backed up in Hong Kong, no single point of failure, and 98% of client virtual assets (VAs) in cold storage. Where controls fall short, the HKMA may add capital, require provisions or impose limits.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPM CA-G-5 Supervisory Review Process (V.7) | HKMA | 19 Dec 2025 | In force | All Authorized Institutions (AIs) | [S:349a543ae2f0, paras 3.6.6, 4.2.8] |
| AML/CFT Guideline for AIs (revised May 2023) | HKMA | 25 May 2023 | In force | AIs, including Registered Institutions (RIs) | [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.1, 2.10-2.11] |
| DLT risk-management considerations (cover letter + Annex) | HKMA | 16 Apr 2024 | In force | AIs (non-binding considerations) | [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]; [S:1884530ff235, Annex] |
| DLT in the Financial Sector: study | HKMA | 19 Mar 2025 | Exploratory | AIs (research, not a rule) | [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction, p.4] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3] |
| Staking from custodial services | HKMA | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1] |
| Updated custody guidance Annex | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 1, 11, 14-19] |
| SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets | HKMA | 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1] |
| Strategic Review of Business Models | HKMA | 9 Mar 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4] |

## Key facts

- Directors and senior managers should understand, across the whole firm, the risks of new or complex activities; CA-G-5 now names cryptoasset activities as an example. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8]
- CA-G-5 notes, "Cryptoasset activities and associated risks are relatively new and evolving." The HKMA may respond to gaps with capital add-ons, provisions for foreseeable losses, limits or other measures. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]
- The HKMA expects each bank's board to oversee and endorse a strategic business plan covering products, revenue models, customer engagement, risk management and operations. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- A bank should spot and weigh the ML/TF risks of new products, business practices, delivery channels and new technologies, before launch, and put mitigants in place. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10-2.11]
- In the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline, the word should is as mandatory as must. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- The April 2024 DLT considerations are non-binding and non-exhaustive; the HKMA reviews whether a bank's systems and controls cover DLT's extra risks, without favouring any technology. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, pp.1-2]
- The board and senior management carry full responsibility for DLT adoption; the bank should update technology-risk, business-continuity and outsourcing policies and keep enough in-house DLT expertise. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 1]
- A bank should justify its choice of network type and check that node operators are trustworthy, reliable and diverse; a permissionless network is likely unsuitable for critical functions without compensating controls. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 2 and 5]
- Business continuity plans for critical DLT use should test DLT scenarios such as cyberattacks, key loss or theft and forks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 10]
- The March 2025 study (input from the SFC, the Insurance Authority and the MPF Schemes Authority; 113 firms surveyed) repeats and expands these points; it is research, not a new rule. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction, p.4]
- For outsourced DLT platforms, the study suggests vetting vendors throughout, contract terms on performance and data security, and backup vendors or failover plans. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Section 4.2.4, item 1, p.48]
- Before launching custody, a bank should complete a full risk assessment, with board and senior-management oversight before and after launch. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]
- VA custody may be delegated only to another AI (or local AI subsidiary), an SFC-licensed VA trading platform, or an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer with HKMA consent for its own coins. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]
- Custody delegate due diligence now covers independent code review and the vendor's release process, with ongoing security and disaster-recovery testing; ultimate responsibility stays with the bank. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 15, 19]
- Key management expectations: tamper-resistant devices such as hardware security modules (HSMs), with HSM vendor due diligence; seeds and keys generated, stored and backed up in Hong Kong; key sharding against single points of failure; readable details for signers. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (b), (i)]
- Where the client assets are VAs, 98% should sit in offline cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8]
- For tokenised products, due diligence on issuers and technology vendors should cover key management, theft and hacking safeguards, smart-contract audits and DLT failure plans. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
- For staking, the bank should keep control of withdrawal keys, check each blockchain protocol, and vet and monitor any third-party staking provider. [S:4641e6c404d2, p.2, section A; pp.2-3, section C]
- CRP-1 requires policies, governance, staff and IT able to assess cryptoasset risk, with documented evidence for each classification available to the HKMA. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Run the ML/TF risk assessment before launching any VA, tokenisation or stablecoin service or new technology. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10-2.11]
- [ ] Brief the board so it understands cryptoasset risks firm-wide and sets limits within risk appetite. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8]
- [ ] Complete a full risk assessment before custody launch, under board oversight. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Update technology-risk, continuity and outsourcing policies for DLT factors. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 1]
- [ ] Apply the para 11 key controls to client VAs, including 98% cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 and fn 8]
- [ ] Monitor custody systems 24/7, test changes before deployment and track dependencies. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23-25]
- [ ] Keep classification evidence for every cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Use the DLT considerations when preparing DLT supervisory submissions. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]
- [ ] Seek HKMA consent where a licensed stablecoin issuer is to hold keys outside Hong Kong for its own coins. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Document due diligence on custody delegates and HSM vendors, and review them regularly. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 11(a), 15]
- [ ] Vet tokenisation platforms and staking providers before use and monitor them after. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3]; [S:4641e6c404d2, section C, p.3]
- [ ] Check that DLT node operators are trustworthy, reliable and diverse. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 5]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline requires an ML/TF risk assessment before any new product or technology launch; should there is mandatory. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.6, 2.10-2.11]
- The DLT considerations are non-binding, but the HKMA asks banks to use them in DLT submissions. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]

**To business heads**
- VA custody can only be outsourced to another bank, an SFC-licensed platform, or a licensed stablecoin issuer (own coins, with consent). [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]
- Tokenised-product launches need issuer and technology-vendor due diligence first. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA expects the board to understand cryptoasset risks and to endorse a digital-transformation business plan. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8]; [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- Weak crypto controls can bring capital add-ons, provisions or activity limits. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Custody keys: HSMs, Hong Kong location, sharding, anti-blind-signing, 98% cold storage for client VAs. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11]
- DLT continuity plans should test key loss, cyberattacks and forks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 10]

## Common mix-ups

- "The DLT considerations are rules with deadlines." They are non-binding and have no deadline; the custody Annex is where the firm numbers sit. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]; [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 8]
- "The March 2025 DLT study sets new rules." It is research that restates the 2024 circular. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction, p.4]
- "Outsourcing custody moves the risk away." Ultimate responsibility stays with the bank. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 19]
- "Hot-wallet insurance must cover 100%." That fixed cover came from the 2024 Annex; the 2026 Annex makes the bank liable and requires adequate financial resources. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- "SFC's VA AML chapter sets our new-product rule." For a bank, the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline governs; RIs only have regard to the SFC chapter. [S:7bfdad704174, Ch.1 fn 1]

## Read these first

1. **Risk management considerations related to the use of DLT (Annex)**, HKMA, 16 Apr 2024. Read all ten items. The HKMA's DLT checklist. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20240416-2-EN/20240416-2-EN.pdf
2. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Custodial Services (Annex)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 1, 10-11, 14-19 and 23-25. Governance, keys and outsourcing in one place. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
3. **SPM CA-G-5 Supervisory Review Process (V.7)**, HKMA, 19 Dec 2025. Read paras 3.6.6 (p.53) and 4.2.8 (p.63). The board-understanding and Pillar 2 hooks. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251217-2-EN/CA-G-5.pdf

## Open items

- The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline for AIs contains no stablecoin, unhosted-wallet or VA red-flag provisions; see D3 for how the gap is handled.
- No general HKMA outsourcing or technology-risk module is in this corpus; only DLT- and custody-specific outsourcing text is covered.
- Two CA-G-5 V.7 copies exist: a November 2025 draft header (placeholder date xx.12.2025) and the 19 December 2025 version. This module cites the 19 December 2025 text; the crypto paragraphs match.

## Related modules
