title: Selling, dealing and advising on virtual assets
md:
For the Head of Compliance at a bank that is also an SFC Registered Institution (RI): after this module you can explain what the joint SFC–HKMA circular regime lets the bank sell, deal in, advise on and stake, and what it must check first.

## In 60 seconds

Since January 2022 the SFC and the HKMA have used one joint circular to set the rules for intermediaries, banks included, that distribute virtual-asset (VA) products or offer VA dealing, advice or portfolio management. The current base text is dated 22 December 2023. A supplemental circular (30 September 2025) and a May 2026 package on licensed stablecoins have since relaxed parts of it. The core ideas stay the same. Most VA-linked products are treated as complex, and most are for professional investors (PIs) only. Clients other than institutional PIs must pass a VA-knowledge test. Actual dealing may only go through SFC-licensed trading platforms. The detailed conduct rules sit in terms and conditions attached to the bank's SFC registration. For a bank, the HKMA is the frontline supervisor, and the HKMA or SFC must be told before any VA activity starts or changes.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities | SFC + HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | Superseded | LCs, RIs | [S:e4828fcba126, p.1] |
| Joint circular (revised) | SFC + HKMA | 20 Oct 2023 | Superseded | LCs, RIs | [S:a37d28d879cf, p.1] |
| Joint circular (current base) + Appendices 1–7 | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 | In force | LCs, RIs | [S:8a016a912528, p.1], [S:0027a8747112, landing page] |
| Supplemental joint circular (staking, off-platform trades, in-kind flows) | SFC + HKMA | 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs, RIs | [S:d5ebca32c92b, p.1] |
| HKMA circular on Relevant Stablecoin activities + Appendix A1 (dealing/advice T&Cs) and A2 (portfolio management T&Cs) | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1], [S:31b4f67e0233, p.1] |
| Letter on Relevant Stablecoin-related activities | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| Circular on Relevant Stablecoin services (26EC26) | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | VATPs, LCs (bank's counterparties) | [S:19d52ade6849, p.1] |
| Guidance on VA financing, shared order book and client VA withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1] |
| Standalone licensing regimes for VA dealing, advisory and management | FSTB + SFC | Dec 2025 / May 2026 | Conclusions published | Banks would register | [S:6186c01c6649, p.1], [S:01c5c5c4045f, p.1] |

## Key facts

- The 22 December 2023 circular replaced both earlier joint circulars in full [S:8a016a912528, para 3].
- VA-related products are those that mainly invest in VAs, get their value mainly from VAs, or track VA returns. The regulators say such products are very likely complex, so suitability applies even without a recommendation [S:8a016a912528, para 5].
- Complex VA-related products should be offered to PIs only, apart from a small group of exchange-traded products [S:8a016a912528, para 6.1]. The exceptions are VA futures on specified exchanges and SFC-authorised VA funds traded on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK). Where there is no solicitation, these can be executed for retail clients without a suitability check, but the knowledge test still applies [S:8a016a912528, paras 7, 9.1].
- Everyone except institutional PIs and qualified corporate PIs should be assessed for VA knowledge. A one-off test is acceptable. A client without the knowledge may trade only after the firm has trained them [S:8a016a912528, para 6.2 and fn 10].
- Dealing must be done with SFC-licensed platforms, either by introducing clients or through an omnibus account, and only for the bank's Type 1 (dealing in securities) clients [S:8a016a912528, paras 17–18].
- Before serving retail dealing clients, a firm should set a net-worth-based VA exposure limit for each client and should restrict them to tokens the platform offers to retail investors [S:8a016a912528, para 20(a)(ii), (iv)].
- Advice on VAs is limited to Type 1 or Type 4 clients. Any VA recommended to a retail client must appear in at least two acceptable indices from two different index providers [S:8a016a912528, paras 26, 28].
- A portfolio triggers the Appendix 7 (RA9) terms if it has a stated VA objective or plans to put 10% or more of gross asset value (GAV) into VAs. Ancillary discretionary VA dealing under Type 1 should stay below 10% of GAV [S:8a016a912528, paras 23–24].
- The September 2025 supplement allows staking for existing VA-dealing clients. The staked assets must sit in segregated accounts at an SFC-licensed platform or an AI [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 4–5].
- The same supplement allows trades through a licensed platform's off-platform (OTC) desk. Paying for or redeeming products with VAs, including in-kind fund flows, does not count as VA dealing [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 6–7].
- The net-worth check and the VA-futures risk disclosure no longer apply to institutional or qualified corporate PIs [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 8–9].
- From May 2026, RIs may deal in a Relevant Stablecoin (a fiat-referenced coin issued under a Stablecoins Ordinance licence) through its licensed issuer as well as through a VATP. Paragraph 20(a)(iii) is removed, so retail omnibus dealing may go through a PI-only VATP if retail clients trade only tokens that VATP has cleared for retail [S:a0bd48559762, para (1)].
- For accounts clearly ring-fenced as Relevant-Stablecoin-only, no knowledge test or exposure limit is needed. Relevant Stablecoin holdings are also left out of the exposure calculation for everyone else [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a)–(b); S:31b4f67e0233, paras 6.2A, 6.4, 6.4A].
- RIs providing VA dealing may now offer VA-backed margin financing, but only to existing securities margin clients. Only bitcoin, ether and Relevant Stablecoins count as eligible collateral, with a haircut of at least 60% on bitcoin and ether [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (2), (4) and fn 5].
- The SFC fined a licensed broker HK$4 million. Between November 2018 and November 2022 it had let retail clients trade 32 VA products that the circulars restricted to PIs, without VA due diligence, knowledge tests or VA warnings [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–4].

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Classify every VA-linked product and apply the PI-only, suitability and knowledge-test rules that follow from that classification [S:8a016a912528, paras 5–10].
- Carry out extra due diligence on any VA fund that is not SFC-authorised, using Appendix 4 [S:8a016a912528, para 12.3].
- Give VA risk disclosures and warning statements to clients other than institutional or qualified corporate PIs [S:8a016a912528, para 15].
- Receive client VAs only through segregated accounts at the partner platform or at an AI that meets HKMA custody standards [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)].
- For Relevant Stablecoins, disclose the coin's stabilisation mechanism and redemption arrangements. Do not let commission rebates be the main reason for a recommendation [S:a0bd48559762, paras (5), (8)].

**Controls & monitoring**
- Have policies, procedures, controls and staff training in place for Relevant Stablecoin activities [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9].
- Keep Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts clearly separate. If another VA is added, the full rules apply, including the knowledge test [S:a0bd48559762, fn 4].
- Keep records on client VAs, orders and staking for at least seven years [S:31b4f67e0233, para 9.7].
- Obtain a signed staking-risk acknowledgement from non-institutional clients before staking [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.1–8.8].
- When relying on VA collateral, monitor its volatility in real time. Book loans secured only by VAs as clean loans for capital purposes [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (5), (9)].

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Give the SFC advance notice of any new VA activity or change to one, including a change in the type of client served, and copy the HKMA where relevant [S:8a016a912528, para 31].
- Notify before the first client VA deposit or withdrawal, the first staking service, or the first VA-funded subscription [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 10].
- A bank that is an AI but not an RI should discuss any Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice or portfolio management with the HKMA before starting [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2].
- Report any actual or suspected material breach of the terms to the SFC and the HKMA as soon as practicable [S:31b4f67e0233, para 12.1].

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Confirm that the platform holds an actual SFC licence. Platforms that are only deemed licensed under AMLO Schedule 3G do not count [S:8a016a912528, para 17 and fn 20].
- Use only an SFC-licensed platform or an AI as the staking service provider. Confirm it has SFC approval or has discussed the service with the HKMA [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.2–8.3].
- For in-kind or VA-funded subscriptions, hold the VAs only at SFC-licensed platforms or AIs, and follow the SFC AML Guideline's VA chapter (Chapter 12) for those transfers [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)–(c)].

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The regime reaches us as an RI through registration conditions that the SFC imposes after consulting the HKMA. The HKMA supervises us day to day [S:8a016a912528, para 19; S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3].
- Our VA anti-money-laundering (AML) baseline remains the HKMA AML Guideline. As an RI we must also have regard to the SFC Guideline's VA chapter (Chapter 12) [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 fn 1].

**To business heads**
- Retail may buy SFC-authorised VA ETFs on the exchange, but only after passing a VA-knowledge test. Overseas spot VA ETPs are still for PIs only [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 9.1].
- Since May 2026, stablecoin-only accounts need no knowledge test and no exposure limit. The account must be ring-fenced and the coin must be HKMA-licensed [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)].

**To the CEO**
- The rules have loosened three times, in 2023, 2025 and 2026. The core safeguards stayed: complex-product treatment, knowledge tests and licensed venues only [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 2; S:a0bd48559762, Background].
- The SFC's January 2026 fine shows that VA distribution failures can be sanctioned years after they happened [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–2].

**To Risk / CRO**
- VA margin lending is now possible, but only against bitcoin, ether and licensed stablecoins. Bitcoin and ether take a haircut of at least 60%, and the VA collateral gets no capital credit [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (4), (9)].
- Discretionary VA exposure under Type 1 should stay below 10% of portfolio GAV [S:31b4f67e0233, para 4.7].

## Common mix-ups

- "All VA products are PI-only." Not so. VA futures on specified exchanges and SFC-authorised VA funds on SEHK can go to retail on an unsolicited basis, but a knowledge test is still needed [S:8a016a912528, paras 7, 9].
- "VA financing is banned." That was true before 2026. Since May 2026, RIs may offer it to margin clients under HKMA conditions [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background and para (1)].
- "The 2026 stablecoin relief covers any stablecoin and any bank." It covers only Relevant Stablecoins and only RIs. It does not cover an issuer dealing in its own coin [S:a0bd48559762, p.2 and fn 3]. AIs that are not RIs are pointed to the same standards by a separate letter [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1].
- "Deleting para 20(a)(iii) only matters for stablecoins." The deletion lets RIs serve retail clients in any VA through PI-only VATPs, as long as each token has been cleared for retail [S:a0bd48559762, para (1)].
- "A 2022 client knowledge test is still good enough." The 2022 and October 2023 circulars are superseded. Only tests done before the December 2023 circular were carried forward [S:8a016a912528, para 3 and fn 40].

## Read these first

1. **Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities**, SFC + HKMA, 22 Dec 2023. Read paras 5–15 (distribution), 16–21 (dealing), 23–28 (management and advice) and 30–31 (implementation). This is the base rulebook. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=23EC66
2. **Supplemental joint circular**, SFC + HKMA, 30 Sep 2025. Read paras 4–10 (staking, OTC, in-kind flows, PI carve-outs, notifications). https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=25EC50
3. **VA-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins**, HKMA to RIs, 27 May 2026. Read Sections I–IV, paras (1)–(17), fn 3–4 and Implementation (p.9). This is the current bank-specific relief and removes para 20(a)(iii). https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The standalone VA dealing, advisory and management licensing regimes are at the conclusions stage. When they commence they will replace the circular-plus-conditions approach, and no grandfathering is planned [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 62–63]. No bill text or commencement date is in the corpus.
- A June 2026 LegCo reply said a bill was planned for later in 2026 [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]. The corpus does not show that it has been introduced.
- The SFC's Statement of Disciplinary Action behind the January 2026 fine is referenced but not in the corpus.
- Canon conflict: the key points for 8a016a912528 still state that financing is prohibited. That was correct for the 2023 text. The May 2026 terms (paras 4.2–4.3) and the HKMA financing circular now allow it for RIs [S:31b4f67e0233; S:e64b7b0267b2].

## Related modules

C2 (VA funds and ETFs), C3 (Custody and key management), C4 (Stablecoins), plus the AML/CFT and VATP modules.

title: VA funds and ETFs
md:
For the Head of Compliance at a bank that distributes funds or acts as participating dealer: after this module you can explain which crypto funds and tokenised funds may be sold in Hong Kong, on what terms, and what the bank checks before it sells, creates or redeems units.

## In 60 seconds

Since October 2022 the SFC has authorised public funds that get exposure to virtual assets (VAs). It began with futures-based ETFs and extended to spot VA ETFs under a December 2023 circular. That circular was revised in April 2025 to permit staking and replaced again on 27 May 2026 (26EC31). A fund with more than 10% of its net asset value (NAV) in VAs needs prior SFC consultation and approval. It may hold only tokens the Hong Kong public can trade on SFC-licensed platforms, must not use leverage, and must keep VAs with an SFC-licensed platform or a bank that meets HKMA custody standards. Separate SFC circulars allow tokenised classes of authorised funds. Since April 2026 they may also be traded on the secondary market on licensed platforms. When a bank sells any of these products, the joint SFC–HKMA circular sets the selling rules. Banks acting as participating dealers must be registered and carry the prescribed terms.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circular on VA futures ETFs (22EC60) | SFC | 31 Oct 2022 | Superseded | Fund managers, distributors | [S:51dac2cabe78, p.1] |
| Circular on SFC-authorised funds with VA exposure (23EC65) | SFC | 22 Dec 2023 | Superseded | Funds, LCs, RIs | [S:5b6530666cc2, p.1] |
| Same circular, revised to add staking (25EC21) | SFC | 7 Apr 2025 | Superseded | Funds | [S:353535602a83, p.1] |
| Same circular, revised (26EC31) | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | Funds, managers, PDs, custodians | [S:c79c4686c5e0, p.1] |
| Tokenisation of SFC-authorised products (26EC22, revising 23EC53) | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | In force | Product providers, distributors | [S:58ea8520974d, p.1] |
| Secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products (26EC23) | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | In force | VATPs, LCs, RIs, product providers | [S:a64e364fd912, p.1] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1] |
| Joint circular (distribution rules) + Sep 2025 supplement | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 / 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs, RIs | [S:8a016a912528, p.1], [S:d5ebca32c92b, p.1] |

## Key facts

- The first VA ETFs allowed were futures-based. They could hold only CME bitcoin and ether futures, and the manager needed at least three years of ETF experience [S:51dac2cabe78, paras 10, 12].
- The 2022 circular also capped net derivative exposure at 100% of NAV and applied the VA-knowledge test to distribution even without solicitation [S:51dac2cabe78, paras 14, 16].
- Under the December 2023 circular, funds could hold spot VAs directly [S:5b6530666cc2, para 1]. The first spot VA ETFs listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange on 30 April 2024 [S:e4236ed2600f, para 1].
- The current circular (26EC31) applies to public funds with more than 10% of NAV in VAs. It replaced the April 2025 version [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 1, 3].
- 26EC31 does not cover fund exposure to Relevant Stablecoins (coins licensed under the Stablecoins Ordinance) or tokenised deposits. Those are dealt with in Q20G of the UT Code FAQs [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 2].
- Eligible VAs are limited to tokens the Hong Kong public can trade on SFC-licensed VATPs. VA futures must trade on conventional regulated futures exchanges, and leverage at fund level is not allowed [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 11, 13, 15].
- Spot VAs are bought and sold through SFC-licensed VATPs, on or off platform, or through AIs that comply with HKMA requirements [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 17 and fn 7].
- Spot ETFs may create and redeem units either in cash or in kind. For in-kind creations, participating dealers (PDs) move VAs into the ETF's custody account at a VATP or an AI. The VAs may have been held locally or overseas [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18].
- PDs for spot VA ETFs must hold an SFC licence or SFC registration, and carry the extra terms in Appendix 6 of the joint circular [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 19 and fn 8].
- The trustee may delegate VA custody only to an SFC-licensed VATP, to an AI that meets HKMA custody standards, or to another entity the SFC accepts. Most assets must be in cold storage, and keys must be kept in Hong Kong [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 20–21].
- The SFC may permit VA funds to stake through VATPs or AIs. Conditions include disclosure of the amount that may be staked, reporting in interim and annual reports, and prior SFC approval [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28, 31]. The SFC caps how much a fund may stake, to keep enough of the portfolio liquid [S:36753b22e10a, para 4].
- On distribution, SFC-authorised VA funds are not PI-only. Units listed on SEHK can be sold execution-only with a knowledge test. Unlisted classes, or trades off exchange, need suitability, warnings and the knowledge test [S:8a016a912528, paras 9.1–9.2 and fn 14].
- The tokenisation circular uses a see-through approach, looking past the token to the underlying product. It permits primary dealing in tokenised authorised products and discourages public permissionless chains unless extra controls are in place [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 13].
- Secondary trading of tokenised funds is permitted for retail through on-screen matching on SFC-licensed VATPs. Controls include a price-deviation alert against the indicative NAV [S:a64e364fd912, paras 8, 12].
- In March 2026, 13 tokenised products were on offer to the Hong Kong public, with tokenised-class assets of about $10.7 billion. The first secondary-trading batch is expected to be tokenised money market funds [S:bbd10edd41cf, paras 4, 7].

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Apply the joint circular's selling rules when distributing any SFC-authorised VA fund, including the knowledge test for all clients except institutional and qualified corporate PIs [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 27; S:8a016a912528, paras 6.2, 9].
- Sell non-authorised VA funds only to PIs, and first do the Appendix 4 due diligence on the manager, the fund and its counterparties [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 12.3].
- As a distributor of tokenised authorised products, apply the usual onboarding and suitability rules [S:58ea8520974d, para 18].
- For tokenised products that are not SFO-regulated (and for tokenised deposits placed by customers), apply the rules for the underlying product. Assess the risks that tokenisation adds [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1].

**Controls & monitoring**
- As a Connecting Broker, show the price-deviation alert, tell clients they can subscribe or redeem at NAV instead, and get their confirmation of the risks before onboarding [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c)].
- Keep an online feed of indicative NAV that refreshes at least once every 15 seconds while the market is trading [S:a64e364fd912, para 20(b)].
- Control online channels so that selling restrictions are enforced [S:8a016a912528, para 11].

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Give the SFC advance notice, and the HKMA too where relevant, before first letting clients subscribe or redeem with VAs, including in-kind flows [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 7(a), 10(d)].
- As an RI, also notify the HKMA before secondary trading in tokenised products [S:a64e364fd912, fn 13].
- Discuss any tokenised-product activity with the HKMA before launch [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6].

**Counterparty due diligence**
- For in-kind flows, hold the VAs only at SFC-licensed platforms or AIs, and apply the SFC AML Guideline Chapter 12 controls to the transfers [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)–(c)].
- Before selling a VA fund, check its custody chain against 26EC31: an approved delegate, mostly cold storage, and keys in Hong Kong [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 20–21].
- On tokenised products, check the key management, smart-contract audits and DLT contingency plans of the issuer and its technology vendor [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3–4].

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The VA fund circular is written for product providers. The bank's own duties as distributor or PD come from the joint circular and our registration terms [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 19, 27].
- For tokenised secondary trading, RIs must notify both regulators. Licensed corporations do not have to notify the HKMA [S:a64e364fd912, fn 13].

**To business heads**
- On-exchange VA ETFs can be sold to retail with a knowledge test. Unlisted classes of the same ETF need full suitability [S:8a016a912528, paras 9.1–9.2, fn 14].
- In-kind creation is allowed, and the VAs may come from overseas holdings. They must land in custody at a VATP or AI [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 17(b)].

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong has moved from futures-only VA ETFs (2022) to spot ETFs, staking and 24/7-style trading of tokenised funds (2026) [S:51dac2cabe78, para 12; S:bbd10edd41cf, para 5].
- Tokenised-class assets were about $10.7 billion across 13 products in March 2026 [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 4].

**To Risk / CRO**
- VA funds must not use leverage at fund level, and custody delegates are limited to VATPs, qualifying AIs, or entities the SFC accepts [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 15, 20].
- Staking by funds needs prior SFC approval and must be reported as a share of NAV, along with revenue and costs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(f), 31].

## Common mix-ups

- "Hong Kong only has futures VA ETFs." Spot exposure has been allowed since the December 2023 circular [S:5b6530666cc2, para 1].
- "A fund holding licensed stablecoins is a VA fund." 26EC31 excludes Relevant Stablecoins and tokenised deposits [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 2].
- "The 2023 or 2025 fund circular still applies." Each was replaced, most recently by 26EC31 on 27 May 2026 [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 3].
- "Tokenised funds can only be subscribed and redeemed." Secondary trading on VATPs has been permitted since 20 April 2026 [S:58ea8520974d, para 6].
- "In-kind subscription makes the bank a VA dealer." The regulators say it does not, but notification, custody and AML conditions apply [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7].

## Read these first

1. **Circular on SFC-authorised funds with exposure to virtual assets (26EC31)**, SFC, revised 27 May 2026. Read paras 2, 11–22, 27–31. These set eligibility, PDs, custody, staking and consultation. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC31
2. **Circular on secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (26EC23)**, SFC, 20 Apr 2026. Read paras 8–15, 19–24 and fn 13. These cover trading channels, Connecting Broker duties and RI notification to the HKMA. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC23
3. **Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities**, SFC + HKMA, 22 Dec 2023. Read paras 5–15 and Appendix 4. These give the distributor's selling rules and fund due diligence. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=23EC66

## Open items

- The exact staking cap for VA funds sits in Q20F of the UT Code FAQs, and Q20G covers stablecoin and tokenised-deposit exposure. Neither is in the corpus [S:c79c4686c5e0, fn 4, fn 11].
- The 22 December 2023 text in the corpus already provides for in-kind creation. The exact date in-kind creation was first permitted cannot be confirmed from the corpus.
- The SFC says it may later widen tokenised secondary trading beyond money market funds. No timeline has been given [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 7].
- The 2026 Policy Address lists stablecoin settlement of tokenised money market funds on licensed VATPs as a stated target [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)].

## Related modules

C1 (Selling, dealing and advising), C3 (Custody and key management), C4 (Stablecoins), plus the tokenisation and Project Ensemble modules.

title: Custody of digital assets and key management
md:
For the Head of Compliance at a bank that holds, or plans to hold, clients' crypto or tokenised assets: after this module you can explain what the HKMA's May 2026 custody standards require, what changed from 2024, how staking fits in, and how the SFC and stablecoin rules set the benchmark for counterparties.

## In 60 seconds

Holding a crypto asset really means controlling the private key that can move it. Custody regulation is therefore mostly about key management. The HKMA set custody standards for banks in February 2024 and replaced them on 27 May 2026 with a longer annex of 26 paragraphs. The new annex keeps the 98% cold-storage rule and the rule that keys stay in Hong Kong. It adds detailed controls on how wallets are operated, drops the fixed insurance percentages, and lets a licensed stablecoin issuer act as custodian of its own coin. The SFC applies parallel and, in places, stricter rules to licensed trading platforms (VATPs). Its August 2025 custody circular is the benchmark it says the future custodian licensing regime will use. That regime reached consultation conclusions in December 2025, and a bill was planned for 2026.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets + Annex | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | Superseded | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:6bccca749ac2, p.1], [S:86e064b2a8d0, p.1] |
| Updated Guidance on Custodial Services + Annex | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.1], [S:ce05e67bcdce, p.1] |
| Staking services for VAs from custodial services | HKMA | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | AIs | [S:4641e6c404d2, landing page] |
| Staking services by VATPs + terms and conditions | SFC | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | VATPs | [S:50bf95ba3143, p.1] |
| VATP Guidelines, Chapter 10 (custody) | SFC | Jun 2023 | In force | VATPs | [S:f1bbafccd556, p.1] |
| Circular on custody of VAs (25EC44) | SFC | 15 Aug 2025 | In force | VATPs and associated entities | [S:562c0f8addce, p.1] |
| Supervision Guideline for licensed stablecoin issuers, para 6.5.7 (keys) | HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed issuers | [S:240be6833157, p.1] |
| VA custodian services licensing regime | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Custodians; banks would register | [S:f41a543388bc, p.1] |

## Key facts

- The 2026 annex applies to client digital assets held by AIs and by subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs. Digital assets here means VAs, tokenised securities and other tokenised assets. Limited purpose tokens and the bank's own holdings are outside it [S:ce05e67bcdce, preamble and fn 1–4].
- The 2026 letter replaces the February 2024 circular. Existing providers are told to review and revise their controls. Unlike 2024, it sets no six-month deadline for confirming compliance [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2; S:6bccca749ac2, Implementation, p.2].
- For client VAs, the annex's key controls are generally required. For other digital assets the bank may take a risk-based approach, but tokens on public permissionless chains call for extra caution [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 chapeau].
- The 98% cold-storage rule for client VAs has not changed [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8; S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 6].
- **Compensation changed.** The 2024 annex asked for insurance or compensation covering 50% of client VAs in cold storage and 100% in hot storage [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. The 2026 annex instead makes the bank liable for losses from incidents attributable to it, backed by adequate financial resources, which may include insurance [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]. The 50%/100% figure now appears only in the SFC's rule for VATPs [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22].
- **Key location.** Keys and seeds must still be generated, stored and backed up in Hong Kong. There is one new exception. With HKMA consent, a bank may appoint an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer to hold that issuer's own coins, with keys in Hong Kong or another location the HKMA accepts [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14(iii)].
- **New operating controls.** These include cold-wallet whitelists with a system check on every transfer, and detection of intrusions into vaults, signing devices and code repositories [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10]. The annex also requires due diligence on HSM vendors, no smart contracts in cold wallets on public chains, segregation of duties over wallet code, dedicated approval devices, air-gapped integrity checks, and prevention of blind signing [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (c), (f), (g), (i)]. Monitoring must run 24/7 [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23].
- **AML section removed.** The 2024 annex had a separate AML/CFT paragraph [S:86e064b2a8d0, para 23]. The 2026 annex has none. The cover letter says meeting the annex does not displace other legal and regulatory requirements [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2].
- Transfers to third parties are now allowed for payment services or client settlement instructions, if effective controls are in place. The definition of client now also covers clients of SFC-licensed VATPs [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m) and fn 9].
- Staking from custody must follow the HKMA's April 2025 guidance, having regard to the SFC's staking terms for VATPs [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 26]. Under the HKMA guidance, the bank keeps control of everything needed to unstake, discloses staking risks such as slashing, and discusses its plans with the HKMA before launch [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–C, Implementation]. VATPs may not use third-party custody for staked assets [S:50bf95ba3143, T&C para 4].
- The SFC's August 2025 circular took effect immediately. It says the weaknesses it describes exist whatever technology is used, whether HSM, MPC or multi-signature. The same standards will be core expectations for future VA custodians [S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2, Way forward p.7].
- Under the custodian regime conclusions, a licence attaches to whoever safekeeps private keys and can move client VAs. Custody of tokenised securities is outside the regime [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6–8, 12]. Non-bank custodians need HK$10 million paid-up capital and HK$3 million liquid capital; banks remain under HKMA capital rules [S:f41a543388bc, para 42]. There will be no grandfathering, but banks already assessed by the HKMA get an expedited process [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51].
- The consultation proposed that banks register with the SFC and that the HKMA be their frontline supervisor [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)].

**Key-management terms, as the documents use them**

- **Hot and cold wallets.** In a hot wallet the private keys sit online, which makes them easier to attack. In a cold wallet they are kept offline [S:8a016a912528, fn 19].
- **HSM (hardware security module).** A tamper-resistant device used to generate and store keys, offline where practicable. Banks must vet the vendor's patching and re-certification [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)].
- **Key sharding and multi-signature.** A key is split among several authorised staff, or several separate keys are required, so that no one individual can ever hold or use the whole key alone; a set number of shard-holders must act together to sign [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(i)]. For stablecoin issuers, the keys in a multi-signature set must be stored in separate, isolated environments [S:240be6833157, para 6.5.7(iv)].
- **MPC (multi-party computation).** Another way of distributing signing power. For licensing, the question is whether the provider can move client assets on its own [S:f41a543388bc, para 11].
- **Blind signing.** Approving a transaction without seeing its contents. Banks must show signers every detail in human-readable form before they sign [S:562c0f8addce, fn 6; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(i)].
- **Whitelisting.** Deposits and withdrawals go only to addresses proved to belong to the client, for example by message signing or a micropayment test. Changes to a cold-wallet whitelist are tightly controlled [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10, 11(m)].
- **Air-gapped signing.** Devices that are never connected to a network, kept in a vault and changed only with physical access. They are used for integrity checks [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(g)]. Stablecoin issuers must generate and use their most important keys in air-gapped environments [S:240be6833157, para 6.5.7(ii), (vii)].

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Keep client assets and wallet addresses segregated from the bank's own. Do not lend, pledge or encumber client assets except for settlement, with prior explicit written consent, or where the law requires it [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 6–7].
- Accept liability for losses attributable to the bank, and hold adequate resources to cover them [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)].
- Disclose the custody arrangements to clients in full. This covers rights on insolvency, segregation, insurance or compensation, commingling, and how forks and airdrops are handled [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 20].

**Controls & monitoring**
- Keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage, and keep keys and backups in Hong Kong [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), (l) and fn 8].
- Train transaction signers in depth and run drills of the business continuity plan [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 3, 5].
- Reconcile each client's holdings regularly against both on-chain and off-chain records, and escalate breaks to senior management [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 21].
- Monitor 24/7, including vendors, protocols, cryptography and common libraries [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24].

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Talk to the HKMA before launching custody, and show that the bank meets the standards [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- Discuss staking plans with the HKMA before launch [S:4641e6c404d2, Implementation, p.3].
- Provide custody records to the HKMA promptly when asked [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 22].

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Delegate VA custody only to another AI (or a local AI's subsidiary), to an SFC-licensed VATP, or, with HKMA consent, to a licensed issuer for its own coins [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14].
- Before onboarding a custodian, have its code reviewed independently and understand how it releases software. After onboarding, test its security, incident reporting and disaster recovery [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15].
- When the counterparty is a VATP, check it against VATP Guidelines paras 10.6–10.8 and 10.22 and against 25EC44 [S:f1bbafccd556; S:562c0f8addce].

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The 2026 annex replaced the 2024 one. The standard for an existing service is to review and revise, but the new wallet controls are expected now [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- AML/CFT for custody still falls under the HKMA AML Guideline, even though the custody annex no longer repeats it [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2; S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3].

**To business heads**
- We can now hold a licensed stablecoin through its issuer as delegate, with HKMA consent [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14(iii)].
- Transfers to third parties for payments and settlement are now allowed if controls are in place [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m)].

**To the CEO**
- The fixed insurance percentages have been replaced by bank liability plus adequate resources, so sizing the exposure is now for us to decide [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)].
- A statutory custodian licence is coming, with no grandfathering. Banks already assessed by the HKMA get an expedited process [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51].

**To Risk / CRO**
- The SFC says choosing HSM, MPC or multi-signature does not by itself remove the vulnerabilities. Process controls decide the outcome [S:562c0f8addce, p.1].
- Staking adds slashing, lock-up and validator risk. The bank must keep the means to unstake [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B].

## Common mix-ups

- "Banks need 50%/100% insurance cover." That was the 2024 rule for banks and remains the rule for VATPs, not for banks from 2026 [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8; S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)].
- "The February 2024 annex is still current." It was superseded on 27 May 2026. One canon entry (86e064b2a8d0) still shows it as in force, which is wrong according to the 2026 letter [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- "Keys may never leave Hong Kong." The general rule stands, but an issuer delegated to hold its own coins may keep keys elsewhere if the HKMA accepts the location [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 7].
- "The custodian regime covers tokenised securities." It does not, because the statutory VA definition excludes securities [S:f41a543388bc, para 12].
- "MPC or HSM equals compliance." The SFC rejects that view [S:562c0f8addce, p.1].

## Read these first

1. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets (Annex)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 6–11 (segregation and safeguarding), 14–17 (delegation) and 23–26 (monitoring and staking). This is the bank's operative custody rulebook. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
2. **Circular to licensed VATP operators on custody of virtual assets (25EC44)**, SFC, 15 Aug 2025. Read Sections I–V (paras 1–24) and the good-practice boxes. It is the benchmark for counterparties and the future custodian regime. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=25EC44
3. **Consultation Conclusions: VA Custodian Services**, FSTB + SFC, 24 Dec 2025. Read paras 6–16 (scope), 25–26 (individuals), 42–51 (capital and transition). https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/Custodian_consultation_conclusion_e.pdf

## Open items

- The corpus has only the BRDR landing page for the HKMA staking circular of 7 April 2025, not the PDF text. Points cited to 4641e6c404d2 rely on the canon summary and should be checked against the PDF.
- The custodian bill was planned for the 2026 LegCo session [S:f41a543388bc, Introduction, p.3]. The corpus does not show it has been introduced, and no commencement date is set [S:f41a543388bc, para 49].
- The SFC will consult separately on whether private VA funds must use SFC-regulated custodians [S:f41a543388bc, para 32].
- The corpus does not say whether a separate custody-specific AML/CFT guidance from the HKMA exists, as the 2024 annex mentioned.

title: Stablecoins
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain Hong Kong's stablecoin law, what a licensed issuer must do, and every role a bank can play: issuer, offeror, dealer or adviser, custodian, or holder on its own balance sheet.

## In 60 seconds

The Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) took effect on 1 August 2025. It requires a Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) licence to issue a fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS) in Hong Kong, or one pegged to the Hong Kong dollar anywhere. Licensed issuers must fully back coins with segregated reserves, redeem at par (normally within one business day), pay no interest and keep keys under tight control. Only listed permitted offerors, including banks, may offer these coins, and retail investors may only get coins from licensed issuers. The HKMA granted the first two licences on 10 April 2026 and says the total will stay very limited. In May 2026 the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) eased how VA conduct rules apply to these Relevant Stablecoins, while keeping advance-notice duties. For its own holdings, a bank classifies stablecoins under the capital rules (CRP-1) and treats them under the liquidity rules (LM-1).

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |

| Discussion Paper on Crypto-assets and Stablecoins | HKMA | 12 Jan 2022 | Superseded | Public; AIs | [S:2b888e600616, Section 6] |
| Consultation paper on stablecoin issuer regime | FSTB + HKMA | 27 Dec 2023 | Superseded | Public | [S:167649d1bc28, para 3] |
| Consultation conclusions | FSTB + HKMA | 17 Jul 2024 | Superseded | Public | [S:54aa01e7396e, para 12.1] |
| Stablecoin issuer sandbox | HKMA | 12 Mar 2024 | Superseded | Would-be issuers | [S:28616d929735, para 1] |
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) | LegCo / HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Issuers; offerors incl. AIs | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| Supervisory Guideline and AML/CFT Guideline for licensed issuers | HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed issuers, incl. an AI licensee | [S:6c3f349e4f90, para 1] |
| Explanatory Note on Licensing | HKMA | Jul 2025 | In force | Applicants | [S:fe4baea8dd7d, Chapter 3] |
| Stablecoin Review Tribunal | FSTB | 1 Nov 2025 | In force | Parties aggrieved by HKMA decisions | [S:16699fe49364, paras 2-3] |

| SPM CRP-1 and LM-1 (V.5) cryptoasset treatment | HKMA | 1 Jan 2026; 19 Dec 2025 | In force | All AIs | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.1]; [S:69600121310a, Annex 3] |
| RI circular and AI letter on Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs; all AIs | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| SFC circular 26EC26 | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | VATPs; LCs | [S:19d52ade6849, para 2] |

## Key facts

- History: HKMA discussion paper (January 2022; its January 2023 conclusions reported 58 submissions); FSTB-HKMA consultation (27 Dec 2023 to 29 Feb 2024); consultation conclusions (17 Jul 2024, 108 submissions). [S:c72a4b732293, para 1.4]; [S:167649d1bc28, para 3]; [S:54aa01e7396e, para 2, p.3]
- The Bill was gazetted on 6 December 2024, passed on 21 May 2025, and the Ordinance commenced on 1 August 2025. [S:a9a82f2b38ce, para 1]; [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 1]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
- A licence is required to issue an FRS in Hong Kong, or an FRS referenced to the Hong Kong dollar anywhere. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]
- Only FRS count as specified stablecoins for now; bank deposits, stored value facility (SVF) float and securities are outside the definition. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 2.1.2, 2.2.1-2.2.2]
- Permitted offerors are: a licensee, an Authorized Institution (AI), an SVF licensee, an SFC-licensed VA trading platform (VATP), or an SFC Type 1 licensed corporation (LC). [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1]
- Permitted offerors may offer licensed-issuer coins to anyone; other specified stablecoins only to professional investors; VA over-the-counter shops are not permitted offerors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), paras 2-3]
- Only advertisements for licensed issuance are allowed, including during the six-month transition. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 3]
- An overseas-incorporated AI may apply without a local subsidiary. The financial-resources and business-activity criteria do not apply to AI applicants. The HKMA's consent is not needed for an AI applicant's controllers or directors. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3; fns 1, 6, 8]
- A licensee must keep paid-up capital of at least HK$25 million; an AI licensee is exempt and follows the Banking Ordinance instead. [S:240be6833157, paras 5.1.1, 5.1.3]
- Reserves must be worth at least the par value of coins in circulation at all times, and must be held on trust with a qualified custodian. Deposits in reserves are capped at three months' tenor, debt securities at one year. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.5.1-2.5.4]
- Valid redemptions are honoured at par without unreasonable fees; generally within one business day unless the HKMA approves otherwise. [S:240be6833157, para 3.3.3]
- Licensees may not pay interest or yield tied to holding a coin. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.13.1]
- Key management covers the whole key lifecycle. Significant keys are generated offline in air-gapped settings. Keys are stored in Hong Kong or another HKMA-accepted location. [S:240be6833157, para 6.5.7(ii), (iv)]
- The issuer AML/CFT Guideline sets a HK$8,000 threshold for customer due diligence and the travel rule. By default, every holder's identity should be verified unless the licensee proves its controls work. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 4.4, 6.5-6.6, 5.11]
- Pre-existing issuers had to apply by 31 October 2025 to keep operating until 31 January 2026. [S:6c3f349e4f90, Explanatory Note on Transitional Provisions, paras 3.3, 4.1]
- The HKMA received 36 first-batch applications and licensed Anchorpoint Financial Limited (FRS01) and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (FRS02), effective 10 April 2026. [S:193316443831, paras 1, 3]; [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- The government says further licences will be very limited and expected launch as early as mid-2026. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (1)-(2)]
- Complaints: the issuer acknowledges within 7 calendar days and responds within 30 (generally no more than 60). The HKMA reviews escalations but does not order compensation. [S:240be6833157, para 8.4.3]; [S:d3e75db3ddb3, Lodging Complaint with the HKMA section]
- The current Stablecoin Review Tribunal panel holds a three-year term running to 31 October 2028; a review must be sought within 30 days of the HKMA decision. [S:16699fe49364, paras 2-3]
- On 28 April 2026 the HKMA warned that tokens using the tickers HKDAP and HSBC were not issued by the licensees, and that neither licensee had yet issued. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2-3]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] As an offeror, offer only licensed-issuer coins to retail; offer other specified stablecoins only to professional investors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 2]
- [ ] Apply the RI standards (Appendices A1 and A2) to Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice and portfolio management. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]
- [ ] Disclose each Relevant Stablecoin's stabilisation and redemption arrangements when dealing. [S:a0bd48559762, para (5), p.5]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Ring-fence Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts; mixing in other VAs brings back full VA rules. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4]
- [ ] Keep advice grounded in the client's use case, not commission rebates. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6]
- [ ] Classify stablecoin holdings under CRP-1 (Group 1b only if all conditions are met; redemption within five calendar days). [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1, 2.3.2]
- [ ] For liquidity (category 1 institutions), treat held stablecoins as non-HQLA debt (generally 0% LCR inflow, 85% NSFR factor); an issuing bank generally applies a 100% outflow. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] RIs: notify the HKMA and SFC before any Relevant Stablecoin activity or material change. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- [ ] All AIs: discuss Relevant Stablecoin services with the HKMA first. [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2]
- [ ] Notify the HKMA before first acquiring a new stablecoin type. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Check an issuer on the HKMA register before dealing. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 5]
- [ ] Custody delegation of stablecoins to a licensed issuer needs that issuer to hold HKMA consent for its own coins. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14 and fn 7]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Banks are permitted offerors; retail may only get licensed-issuer coins. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1]; [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 2]
- RIs notify the HKMA and SFC before Relevant Stablecoin activity; other AIs discuss with the HKMA first. [S:a0bd48559762, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.2]

**To business heads**
- Two issuers are licensed (effective 10 April 2026); the HKMA says numbers will stay very limited. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:193316443831, final paragraphs]
- Relevant-Stablecoin-only dealing needs no Type 1 registration and no VA knowledge test for ring-fenced accounts. [S:a0bd48559762, paras (2), (3)(a)]

**To the CEO**
- An AI can apply to issue and is exempt from some criteria, such as capital and business-activity limits. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, fns 1, 8]
- Launch of the first licensed coins was expected from mid-2026. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (1)]

**To Risk / CRO**
- A held stablecoin is non-HQLA debt for liquidity; an issuing bank faces a 100% LCR outflow. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]
- HKMA-licensed coins are deemed to meet CRP-1's permissionless-chain measures, but still need conditions 1-4. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.6.3]

## Common mix-ups

- "A Relevant Stablecoin is an investment product." The HKMA letter says its guidance should not be read that way. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]
- "Sandbox firms are licensed." Sandbox admission was not a licence; the HKMA later said it is neither a precondition nor a guarantee. [S:28616d929735, para 9]; [S:e0b249a7eb8c, Licensing regime section, para 5]
- "A licence means coins are live." Both licensees confirmed on 28 April 2026 they had not yet issued. [S:275e7319a841, para 3]
- "The SFC's 26EC26 governs our bank." It covers VATPs and LCs; RIs follow the HKMA RI circular. [S:19d52ade6849, para 2]; [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]
- "Only Hong Kong firms are caught." HKD-referenced coins issued anywhere need a licence. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]
- "The HKMA will get my client compensated." It does not order issuers to pay compensation. [S:d3e75db3ddb3, Lodging Complaint with the HKMA section]

## Read these first

1. **Explanatory Note on Licensing of Stablecoin Issuers**, HKMA, Jul 2025. Read Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 (especially 3.2-3.5 and 3.13). Scope, offerors, criteria and AI carve-outs. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/stablecoin-issuers/Explanatory_Notes_on_Licensing_of_Stablecoin_Issuers_eng.pdf
2. **Guideline on Supervision of Licensed Stablecoin Issuers**, HKMA, 1 Aug 2025. Read sections 2-3, 6.5 and 8.4. Reserves, redemption, keys and complaints. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/stablecoin-issuers/Guideline_on_supervision_of_licensed_stablecoin_issuers_eng.pdf
3. **VA-related activities in relation to Relevant Stablecoins (RI circular)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read all nine pages. How a bank deals, advises and distributes. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The corpus has no official confirmation that either licensee had launched a regulated stablecoin by 25 Sep 2026.
- The HKMA has made no decision on the number or timing of further licences. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)]
- The CRP-1 text is still to be updated for the June 2026 clarification of para 2.6.4 (tokenised assets, not stablecoins). [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- The 2026 Policy Address says the SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms; no detailed measures are in the corpus. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- Statutory text of Cap. 656 on e-Legislation is not in the corpus; section numbers here come from HKMA documents.

title: Tokenisation: tokenised products, deposits and bonds
md:
For a bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After reading, you can explain which tokenisation rules bind the bank today, which HKMA projects the bank may join, and what is still only a stated plan.

## In 60 seconds

Tokenisation records a claim on a real asset (bond, fund unit, gold, bank deposit) on a distributed ledger (DLT). Regulators apply the rules of the underlying product to its tokenised form, plus extra checks for technology, custody and legal risk. For banks, the HKMA's February 2024 circular sets those expectations, and the SFC's circulars cover tokenised securities and tokenised SFC-authorised funds. On the infrastructure side, the HKMA runs Project Ensemble, which moved in November 2025 into a live pilot (EnsembleTX) where seven named banks settle real-value tokenised-deposit transactions. The Government has also issued three digital green bonds, and the Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) issued a digital bond in June 2026. The next steps (24/7 central-bank-money settlement, a CMU OmniClear digital-asset platform, tokenised Exchange Fund Bills tests, and a second-phase legal review) are stated targets in the 2026 Policy Address, not rules.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Circular on tokenisation of SFC-authorised investment products (original) | SFC | 2 Nov 2023 | Superseded | Product providers, distributors | [S:d422282a262d, p.1 banner] |
| Circular on tokenisation of SFC-authorised investment products (revised) | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | In force | Product providers; LC/RI distributors | [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5-6] |

| Government digital green bonds: ~HK$6bn (Feb 2024); ~HK$10bn with e-HKD/e-CNY settlement option (Nov 2025) | HKSAR Govt / HKMA | 7 Feb 2024; 10 Nov 2025 | Issued, effective Feb 2024 / Nov 2025 | Investors | [S:4290ec1111e3, key features]; [S:ac6cd085a325, paras 1-5] |

| Tokenised Bond Expert Group (TBEG) | HKMA | 5 Jun 2026 | Exploratory | Industry members | [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-3] |
| FSTB/HKMA DLT fixed-income review, phase 1 (incl. Companies Registry FAQs on DLT debenture registers) | FSTB + HKMA | 29 Jun 2026 | Conclusions published | Bond issuers, arrangers | [S:279f10054c6e, 'Issuing clarifications' section] |
| Phase 2 legal review (e-execution, possession/transfer of tokens) | FSTB + HKMA/TBEG | H2 2026 | Stated target | Market | [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase']; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iii)] |

Note: 'Issued' on bond rows marks a completed one-off transaction, not a rule.

## Key facts

- The HKMA circular covers tokenised real-world assets (e.g. non-SFO structured products, spot precious metal). It excludes stablecoins and SFO-regulated instruments, but also applies to customers placing tokenised deposits. It expects due diligence on issuer and vendor, plain-language risk disclosure, HKMA custody standards where relevant, and prior discussion with the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 fn 1; Sections A-D; p.6]
- General principle: the existing selling and investor-protection rules for a product also apply to its tokenised form; AIs should still assess whether tokenisation changes the product's nature (e.g. fractional interests becoming a collective investment scheme). [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.2]
- The SFC treats tokenised securities as traditional securities in a tokenisation wrapper. Complex-product status is judged on the underlying security, and the 2019 professional-investor-only restriction was lifted. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 21, 24, 26]
- Registered institutions (RIs) planning digital-securities activity should notify both the SFC and the HKMA in advance. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and footnote 8]
- For tokenised SFC-authorised funds, primary dealing is allowed. Product providers remain responsible for the tokenisation arrangement, and should not use public-permissionless chains without extra controls such as a permissioned token. [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 10, 13]
- Since 20 April 2026, secondary trading of these products on SFC-licensed VATPs is allowed with fair-pricing controls; RIs engaging in it must also notify the HKMA. [S:a64e364fd912, para 12 and footnote 13]
- Project Ensemble centres on tokenised deposits (digital representations of commercial bank deposits). [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] EnsembleTX moved Ensemble from proof-of-concept to real-value transactions. It starts with tokenised money market fund and treasury use cases, with interbank settlement via HKD RTGS first. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3]
- The HKMA lists seven Tokenised Deposit Banks for EnsembleTX: Bank of China (Hong Kong), China Construction Bank (Asia), Fubon Bank (Hong Kong), Fusion Bank, Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong), The Bank of East Asia and HSBC. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A]
- Tokenised deposits that are a legal claim on the bank can be reported like ordinary deposits for the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR), but never get the 3%/5% stable-deposit outflow rate. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]
- The DBGS pays 50% of eligible costs: up to HK$1.25m (Half Grant) or HK$2.5m (Full Grant), for at most two issuances per issuer group. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1]
- For the Full Grant, the DLT platform provider must not be an associate of the issuer. The issue must also be at least HK$1bn, go to five or more unrelated investors, and be listed on SEHK or an SFC-licensed VATP. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3]
- The FSTB/HKMA phase-1 review found the current legal framework flexible enough for tokenised bonds. The Companies Registry confirmed that a DLT register of debenture holders can meet Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) record-keeping rules. [S:279f10054c6e, opening para and 'Issuing clarifications' section]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Apply existing product-selling rules to tokenised products, plus the tokenisation-specific expectations. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.2]
- Apply the circular's standards when customers place tokenised deposits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1]
- As distributor of tokenised SFC-authorised products, act as a regulated intermediary under existing conduct and suitability rules. [S:58ea8520974d, para 18]

**Controls & monitoring**
- Carry out ongoing due diligence on the tokenised product, its issuer and technology vendors, including key management and audits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A]
- Give customers plain-language tokenisation risk disclosures. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section B]
- If providing custody, meet the HKMA custody standards. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section D]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss tokenised-product plans with the HKMA before launch. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Implementation', p.6]
- As an RI, notify the SFC and the HKMA before digital-securities activity. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35, footnote 8]
- As an RI in secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products, also notify the HKMA. [S:a64e364fd912, footnote 13]
- Optional: use the Supervisory Incubator for DLT to confirm risk management before full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Assess the tokenisation platform's track record, key-management and ownership-record controls. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
- For bonds you arrange or hold: check the settlement system and the legal-finality position (CMU settlement has statutory finality). [S:4290ec1111e3, footnote 2]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Tokenised products are not a new licence category. Existing product rules apply, plus HKMA tokenisation due diligence and disclosure, and advance discussion with the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.2-6]
- Our RI must tell both the SFC and the HKMA before digital-securities or tokenised-fund secondary-trading work. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, fn 8]; [S:a64e364fd912, fn 13]

**To business heads**
- EnsembleTX runs throughout 2026 with real-value tokenised-deposit settlement. The HKMA invites banks with real use cases to take part. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 2-3 and CE remarks]
- The DBGS can refund up to HK$2.5m per issue, but not if the issuer uses an associated DLT platform. [S:5a0563de8142, ss.1, 3]

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong has done three Government digital bond issues, the latest about HK$10bn. The HKMC added about HK$12bn in June 2026. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5]; [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1]
- The Policy Address targets CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation for EnsembleTX around end-2026, and a CMU OmniClear digital-asset platform this year. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(iv), 50]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Tokenised deposits do not get stable-deposit liquidity treatment. If holders cannot always be identified, outflows are reported separately. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]
- The HKMA expects DLT risk management covering network choice, smart contracts, settlement finality and key security. [S:1884530ff235, Annex items 2-8]

## Common mix-ups

- 'Tokenised securities are automatically complex or professional-investor-only.' They are not. The SFC looks through to the underlying security and dropped the 2019 PI-only restriction. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 24, 26]
- 'The HKMA tokenised-products circular covers stablecoins.' It expressly does not. [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1]
- 'Secondary trading of tokenised SFC funds is still barred.' That was the 2023 position. The revised April 2026 framework allows it on SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:d422282a262d, paras 6-7]; [S:58ea8520974d, para 6]
- 'EnsembleTX is not an official name.' It is used in the HKMA's own November 2025 announcement and annex. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 1]; [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A]

## Read these first

1. **Sale and distribution of tokenised products**, HKMA, 20 Feb 2024. Read the whole circular (6 pages), especially Sections A-D and 'Implementation'. It is the bank's baseline rulebook. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20240220-10-EN/20240220-10-EN.pdf
2. **Circular on secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products**, SFC, 20 Apr 2026. Read paras 8-24 and footnote 13 for RI duties. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC23
3. **EnsembleTX announcement and Annexes A/B**, HKMA, 13 Nov 2025. Read the full release and both annexes to see pilot scope and participants. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251113-3/ and https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2025/20251113e3a1.pdf

title: Financing, shared order books and client withdrawals
md:
For a bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets) whose Registered Institution (RI) offers, or plans to offer, virtual asset (VA) dealing. After reading, you can explain what the SFC changed in February 2026, how the HKMA applied it to banks in May 2026, and which controls must be in place first.

## In 60 seconds

Until February 2026, brokers and banks dealing in VAs for clients could not lend clients money to buy VAs. On 11 February 2026 the SFC let VA brokers that already do securities margin lending extend VA financing to existing margin clients. Collateral in VA form is limited to bitcoin and ether, with a haircut of at least 60%. On 27 May 2026 the HKMA let RIs do the same on equivalent terms. It also allowed HKMA-licensed stablecoins as collateral and required loans backed only by VA to be treated as clean (unsecured) loans for capital. The same packages let clients reach a VA trading platform's (VATP's) shared order book, which pools liquidity with overseas affiliate platforms. Retail clients get access only after an explicit opt-in. They also set anti-fraud controls where clients can withdraw VAs. The rules bind LCs through the SFC and RIs through the HKMA as frontline regulator.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circular on shared liquidity by VATPs (25EC56) + Shared Order Book terms and conditions | SFC | 3 Nov 2025 | In force | SFC-licensed VATPs (prior SFC approval needed) | [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 3, 26]; [S:fda3c03f239d, para 3] |
| Circular on VA brokers: financing, shared order book, client VA withdrawals (26EC5) | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | In force | LCs dealing in VA via omnibus accounts | [S:73dac3a5a832, para 1] |
| Circular permitting VATPs to accept affiliated market makers (26EC6) | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | In force | SFC-licensed VATPs | [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9] |
| Guidance on offering of financing for VA dealing, shared order book and client VA withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | All RIs providing VA dealing | [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1] |
| VA-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins (revised terms and conditions) | HKMA (formulated with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:553c7d718bec, landing page] |
| SFC consultation on capital requirements for VA activities incl. VA financing | SFC | not dated | Stated target ('in due course') | LCs | [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14] |

## Key facts

- Before 11 February 2026, neither LCs nor RIs could give clients financial accommodation to acquire VA under the omnibus-account terms and conditions. [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background, p.1]
- The SFC framed VA financing as a first step under Pillar P of its ASPIRe roadmap. It is limited to VA brokers that already provide securities margin financing. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 3-5]
- The HKMA allows RIs providing VA dealing to offer VA financing if they observe standards similar to the SFC's. It restates those standards for RIs as items (1)-(9). [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'HKMA's guidance for RIs', p.2]
- Eligible borrowers are only the RI's existing securities margin clients. Credit limits should not rise just because VA financing is available. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (2)-(3)]
- Where a client's VA holdings count toward financial capability, the RI should assess seven risk factors. These include price-gap risk, digital-asset sector concentration and correlation with equities under stress. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3)(a)-(g)]
- If an RI chooses to rely on VA collateral, it is limited to bitcoin, ether and stablecoins issued under HKMA licences ('Relevant Stablecoins'), with a prudent haircut. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4)]
- The haircut for bitcoin and ether should be 60% or more. The HKMA may revise it on prior notice. No numeric haircut is set for Relevant Stablecoins. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4) and footnote 5]
- Collateral is generally valued at prices on the VATP where the client's orders execute (or, for Relevant Stablecoins, the licensed issuer). RIs should keep a contingency plan for VATP outages. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6) and footnote 6]
- VA financing counts as part of the margin loan book. Concentration controls cover VA collateral, and VA collateral may not be repledged or reused except on client default. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(a)-(c)]
- If the loan exceeds collateral value, or a client has an outstanding margin call and a poor payment record, the RI should suspend advances, stop VA purchases on margin and review the client's limits. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (8)]
- Because the Banking (Capital) Rules do not treat VA as eligible collateral, loans secured solely by VA must be treated as clean loans to the client. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9)]
- For LCs, VA collateral gets a 100% haircut under the Financial Resources Rules until the SFC consults on revised capital rules. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14]
- Tokenised products fall outside this circular. The financing ban does not apply to them, and RIs follow the HKMA's February 2024 tokenised-products circular instead. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4]
- A shared order book lets an SFC-licensed VATP integrate its order book with affiliated overseas platforms. The overseas platform must be in a FATF or FATF-style regional body member jurisdiction with aligned regulation. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 3, 7]
- VATPs operating a shared order book should accept only fully pre-funded orders, settle on delivery-versus-payment, and hold a Hong Kong reserve fund on trust at least equal to the Unsettled Trade Limit. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 10, 13, 17]
- RIs doing agency trading on a shared order book, or offering retail access, follow SFC 26EC5 paras 15-17. Before trading they assess conflicts, settlement, default handling, reserve funds and client recourse. Retail access needs a prominent risk explanation and an express election. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 16-17]
- Where client VAs stay in custody at the VATP, a withdrawal function adds cyber risk: a compromised broker system could send fraudulent withdrawal instructions. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 19]
- RIs permitting withdrawals must apply SFC 26EC5 paras 18-20 on top of HKMA e-banking and technology-risk rules. These cover robust authentication, round-the-clock monitoring with suspension, and working with VATPs on withdrawal limits. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20]
- 26EC6 lets a VATP accept an affiliated market maker, subject to conditions. These include functional independence, client-order priority at the same price, post-trade identification and disclosure. The VATP must notify the SFC first with an independent firm's report. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9-10]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Offer VA financing only to existing securities margin clients, on financial capability and posted collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(2)]
- Book VA-only-secured loans as clean loans for capital. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9)]
- Do not repledge, reuse or encumber VA collateral except on default. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(c)]

**Controls & monitoring**
- Document VA risk-assessment methods in the margin lending policy, and monitor vulnerable VA exposures on an ongoing basis. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(a)]
- Keep real-time capability to monitor VA collateral volatility and act promptly. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(b)]
- Set margin-call and stop-advance triggers, and act on them. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (8)]
- For withdrawals: monitor continuously, with escalation and suspension also outside office hours. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20(b)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- The circular itself sets no new notification step. For new VA activity, the HKMA's standing expectation is to discuss plans before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body para 5]
- Contacts for queries are named in the circular, by topic. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Before shared order book trading, assess the operators' conflicts of interest, the settlement mechanism, failure and default processes, reserve fund and insurance, and client recourse. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 16]
- Agree withdrawal limits and suspicious-withdrawal blocking with the partner VATP. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20(c)]
- Keep an outage contingency plan for the VATP used to value collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6)]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The HKMA's 27 May 2026 circular lets our RI offer VA margin financing on SFC-equivalent terms. Collateral is limited to bitcoin, ether and HKMA-licensed stablecoins. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(4)]
- Withdrawal and shared-order-book standards come from SFC 26EC5 paras 15-20, applied to RIs by the HKMA. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]

**To business heads**
- Only existing securities margin clients qualify, and limits should not rise just because VA financing exists. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (2)-(3)]
- Retail clients can use a shared order book only after an explained overseas-risk warning and an express opt-in. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 17]

**To the CEO**
- This is a regulator-described first step to bring margin trading into VA, aimed at liquidity with risk controls. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 3]
- The HKMA gives VA collateral no capital credit, so VA-backed lending carries clean-loan capital. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9)]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Bitcoin and ether collateral needs at least a 60% haircut. Stablecoin haircuts are left to the RI's prudent judgement. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), footnote 5]
- The HKMA warns that VAs have a limited track record in systemic shocks and can fall sharply within a day. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3)]

## Common mix-ups

- 'The SFC circular binds banks directly.' It binds LCs. Banks, as RIs, are brought in by the HKMA's 27 May 2026 circular. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 1]; [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2]
- 'Bank collateral rules are identical to the SFC's.' The HKMA adds Relevant Stablecoins as eligible collateral and uses Banking (Capital) Rules clean-loan treatment rather than the Financial Resources Rules 100% haircut. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (4), (9)]; [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 7, 14]
- 'The financing ban covered tokenised products.' It never did. The HKMA says the prohibition does not apply to acquiring tokenised products. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4]
- 'A shared order book can link to any overseas exchange.' At this stage it is limited to intra-group (affiliated) platforms. [S:f009f1a6d615, para 3]

## Read these first

1. **Guidance on Offering of Financing for VA Dealing, Shared Order Book, and Client VA Withdrawals**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read all six pages, especially items (1)-(9) and page 6. It is the bank-binding text. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-1-EN/20260527-1-EN.pdf
2. **Circular on licensed corporations providing VA dealing services (26EC5)**, SFC, 11 Feb 2026. Read paras 14-20, the text the HKMA incorporates. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC5
3. **Circular on shared liquidity by VATPs (25EC56)**, SFC, 3 Nov 2025. Read paras 3-18 and 25-26 to understand the partner platform's settlement risk. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=25EC56

## Open items

- Paragraph-number conflict: SFC 26EC5 cites the financing ban as para 4.4 of the omnibus terms and conditions. The HKMA cites para 4.3 'as renumbered on 30 September 2025'. Both are official. Check the revised terms attached to the HKMA stablecoin circular of 27 May 2026 for the current numbering. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 2]; [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1 footnote 3]
- Date discrepancy: the HKMA's footnote 4 dates the joint circular 23 December 2023. The SFC's version is dated 22 December 2023. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4]; [S:8a016a912528, p.1]
- The SFC capital-requirements consultation for VA activities has no published date. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14]
- The revised terms and conditions (appendices to the HKMA's 27 May 2026 stablecoin circular) are catalogued, but their full text was not reviewed for this module. [S:553c7d718bec, landing page]
- No numeric haircut is specified for Relevant Stablecoin collateral.
