title: VATP counterparties and the SFC platform regime
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain how the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licenses virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs), what the rulebook requires of them, and how to use that rulebook when a platform is your bank's partner, customer or counterparty.

## In 60 seconds

Since 1 June 2023, any platform running a virtual asset (VA) exchange in Hong Kong, or actively marketing one to Hong Kong investors, needs an SFC licence under Part 5B of the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO). Before that, the SFC only had an opt-in route for platforms that listed at least one security token. The SFC's VATP Guidelines are the platforms' rulebook: token admission, retail gates, 98% cold storage, compensation cover and key prohibitions. They bind platforms, not banks. But a bank that deals in VAs for clients may only do so through SFC-licensed platforms, so the Guidelines become your due-diligence benchmark. Since late 2025 the SFC has widened what platforms may do, and the HKMA has told registered institutions (RIs) which related SFC rules they must follow.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Position paper: opt-in regulation of VATPs | SFC | 6 Nov 2019 | Superseded | Platforms listing a security token | [S:024089b01825, paras 32, 82] |
| AMLO Part 5B VATP licensing regime | LegCo / SFC | 1 Jun 2023 | In force | All VATPs in or marketing to Hong Kong | [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1] |
| Guidelines for VATP Operators | SFC | Jun 2023 | In force | Licensed VATPs; bank uses as benchmark | [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2] |
| Lists of VATPs (licensed, applicants, removed, closing-down) | SFC | live; update 29 May 2026 | In force | Public; counterparty checks | [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table] |
| Inspection findings on deemed applicants (circular 25EC3) | SFC | 16 Jan 2025 | In force | Platform Operators and applicants | [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1] |
| Custody circular for licensed VATPs | SFC | 15 Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed VATPs | [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7] |
| Expansion of products and services; shared liquidity | SFC | 3 Nov 2025 | In force | Licensed VATPs | [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5]; [S:f009f1a6d615, para 26] |
| Affiliated market makers (AFMM) | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | In force | Licensed VATPs | [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9] |
| High-level framework for perpetual contracts | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | In force | Licensed VATPs; professional investors only | [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors' and 'Way forward' sections] |
| Guidance to RIs on VA financing, shared order book, VA withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs (banks) | [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6] |
| Phishing-resistant authentication circular | SFC | 9 Jul 2026 | Issued, effective 8 Jul 2027 | Internet brokers and SFC-licensed VASPs | [S:724f4d9f786e, para 21(c)] |

## Key facts

- In 2018 the SFC chose to observe selected platforms in its Regulatory Sandbox before deciding whether to license any. [S:e7f89463ceae, Section II]
- Under the 2019 position paper, the SFC could only license a centralised Hong Kong platform that traded at least one security token; platforms trading only non-security tokens sat outside its powers. [S:024089b01825, paras 4, 32]
- The SFC granted the first VATP licence in December 2020, for Type 1 and Type 7 regulated activities, limited to professional investors. [S:60682e9fd7fa, main text and Note 1, p.1]
- The AMLO regime started on 1 June 2023 and requires every platform running a VA exchange in Hong Kong, or actively marketing one to Hong Kong investors, to be SFC-licensed. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1]
- Pre-existing platforms could keep operating until 31 May 2024; those that applied by 29 February 2024 and met the conditions were deemed licensed from 1 June 2024. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 12]
- Deemed status is not a licence. In the SFC's words, such platforms are "NOT formally licensed by the SFC", and they should not onboard new retail clients before proving their controls. [S:c787f990209d, 'Reminder for investors' and 'Reminder for deemed-to-be-licensed VATP applicants']
- The SFC publishes lists of licensed platforms, applicants, removed applicants and closing-down platforms; at 29 May 2026 the licensed list showed 13 platforms, and listing does not guarantee creditworthiness. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table and note]
- Token admission: a platform should run a token admission and review committee and do documented due diligence before listing any token. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.6]
- Retail access: a token offered to retail clients should be highly liquid, meaning included in at least two acceptable indices from at least two different index providers. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.7-7.8]
- Custody: a platform and its Associated Entity should keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage, and hold an SFC-approved compensation arrangement covering 50% of cold-storage and 100% of hot-storage client VAs. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22]
- Prohibitions: the Guidelines say platforms should not finance client VA purchases, deal in VA futures or derivatives, run algorithmic trading for clients, use client VAs to generate returns, trade for their own account, or make markets on a proprietary basis. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.24-7.26, 13.2-13.4]
- After inspecting all deemed applicants on cybersecurity, client-asset safeguarding and know-your-client (KYC) processes, the SFC told every Platform Operator to review its systems and fix gaps at once. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]
- In November 2025 the SFC dropped the 12-month track record for tokens offered to professional investors, and for stablecoins from licensed issuers offered to retail; it still applies to other retail tokens. [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5]
- Shared liquidity: licensed platforms may, with prior written SFC approval, share an order book with affiliated overseas platforms, starting with intra-group liquidity only. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 3, 26]
- Since February 2026 a platform may let an affiliated market maker trade on it, after notifying the SFC and filing an independent firm's report; client orders keep priority at the same price. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7(e), 9]
- The SFC's perpetual-contracts framework limits these products to professional investors, and margin must be fiat, or HKMA-regulated stablecoins or tokenised deposits. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets' and 'Margin arrangements' sections]
- The SFC named JPEX as unregulated, said it was placed on the SFC Alert List in July 2022, said it never applied for a licence, and referred the matter to the Police on suspicion of fraud. [S:c8dcca119dab, main text, paras 3, 5-6]
- The SFC expects SFC-licensed VASPs to adopt phishing-resistant login and device binding by 8 July 2027; it does not treat one-time passwords (OTPs) as phishing-resistant. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] If the bank offers VA dealing, partner only with SFC-licensed platforms, via an omnibus account or by introducing clients. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- [ ] Offer VA dealing only to clients of the bank's Type 1 (dealing in securities) business. [S:8a016a912528, para 18]
- [ ] As an RI, follow the SFC's shared-order-book guidance when trading for clients on such a book or giving retail clients access. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6]
- [ ] As an RI permitting client VA withdrawals, apply the SFC's withdrawal safeguards on top of HKMA e-banking and technology rules. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Re-check a platform's status on the live SFC lists before onboarding and at review; the lists can lag between updates. [S:dddd919625e9, Note 1]; [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section Note 1]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Give the SFC, and the HKMA where relevant, advance notice before starting or changing VA activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] When banking a VASP, assess its business model, licensing status and AML/CFT controls, with correspondent-style due diligence. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- [ ] For a VASP located outside Hong Kong, find out whether the account serves its own use or its clients; if clients, apply the correspondent-banking measures. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24]
- [ ] Benchmark a partner platform against the VATP Guidelines: token committee, retail index test, 98% cold storage, compensation cover. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22]
- [ ] Ask whether the platform has fixed the gaps in the SFC's inspection findings. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The VATP Guidelines bind platforms, not the bank. For us they are a due-diligence yardstick, because our VA dealing must run through SFC-licensed platforms. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2]; [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- On our own AML duties for VASP customers, we follow the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline, including correspondent-style checks on overseas VASPs. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24]

**To business heads**
- Shared order books and affiliated market makers are now allowed for platforms, with SFC approval or notice; perpetuals are professional-only. [S:f009f1a6d615, para 26]; [S:84b3c1a0cee1, para 9]; [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets']
- If we give clients access to a platform's shared order book, the HKMA expects us to follow the SFC's broker guidance. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6]

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong moved from an opt-in, professional-only model (2019-2020) to mandatory licensing for all platforms from June 2023. [S:024089b01825, para 32]; [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1]
- The SFC’s licensed list showed 13 platforms at 29 May 2026. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table]

**To Risk / CRO**
- The Guidelines say licensed platforms should hold 98% of client VAs cold and carry compensation cover of 50% cold and 100% hot. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22]
- The SFC's inspections of deemed applicants covered cybersecurity, client assets and KYC; it ordered immediate fixes. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]

## Common mix-ups

- "Deemed licensed means vetted." No: the SFC says it never checked whether deemed platforms are fit and proper, and they may never get a licence. [S:dddd919625e9, Note 4]
- "The 50%/100% compensation rule applies to our custody." It is a VATP rule; the HKMA's custody annex for banks uses a different approach. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22]; [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- "SMS OTP is enough." The SFC does not consider OTP phishing-resistant for login or device binding. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 7]

## Read these first

1. **Guidelines for Virtual Asset Trading Platform Operators** — SFC, June 2023. Read paras 7.1-7.8 (token admission, retail test), 7.24-7.26, 10.6, 10.11, 10.22 and 13.2-13.4. This is your benchmark for any platform counterparty. https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/assets/components/codes/files-current/web/guidelines/Guidelines-for-Virtual-Asset-Trading-Platform-Operators/Guidelines-for-Virtual-Asset-Trading-Platform-Operators.pdf
2. **Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities** — SFC and HKMA, 22 Dec 2023. Read paras 17-18 and 31. Explains why bank VA dealing must go through licensed platforms. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=23EC66
3. **Lists of virtual asset trading platforms** — SFC, live page (29 May 2026 update in corpus). Read the licensed table and the applicant-list notes. The only reliable status check. https://www.sfc.hk/en/Welcome-to-the-Fintech-Contact-Point/Virtual-assets/Virtual-asset-trading-platforms-operators/Lists-of-virtual-asset-trading-platforms

## Open items

- The appendices to the January 2025 inspection circular (standards A-V and findings) are not in the corpus text; only the cover letter was checked. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]
- The perpetuals framework is an initial approach that the SFC says may be refined; no approvals of specific perpetual products appear in the corpus. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Way forward']
- The SFC press release is dated 16 Dec 2020, while the licensed list shows a licence date of 15/12/2020 for the earliest platform; the corpus does not explain the one-day gap. [S:60682e9fd7fa, dateline]; [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table]

title: Capital and prudential treatment of cryptoassets
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain how Hong Kong turned the Basel cryptoasset standard into binding capital, liquidity and exposure rules, how a cryptoasset gets classified, and what the bank must notify to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).

## In 60 seconds

The global bank standard setter, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), published a standard on banks' cryptoasset exposures in December 2022 and amended it in July 2024. The HKMA consulted on it (CP 24.01, 2024), sent draft rules to the industry in January 2025, and the government gazetted three sets of amendment rules in July 2025. The rules, plus a new guidance module CRP-1 and nine revised modules, took effect on 1 January 2026. Every cryptoasset a bank holds is sorted into Group 1a (tokenised traditional assets), 1b (stablecoins that pass strict tests), 2a (Group 2 assets that meet hedging criteria, so some hedges count) or 2b (everything else, at a 1,250% risk weight). New cryptoasset types must be notified to the HKMA and sit in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees otherwise. In June 2026 the HKMA eased one Group 1 condition for tokenised assets on permissionless chains.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

## Key facts

- CP 24.01 proposed bringing the December 2022 Basel standard into Hong Kong rules no earlier than 1 July 2025, with comments due by 6 May 2024. [S:27f8bc2f6b2a, paras 2, 4, 11]
- In January 2025 the HKMA sent draft rule amendments to the industry, asking for comments by 20 February 2025 and aiming for a 1 January 2026 start to match Basel. [S:ebc5f9b5ee0d, p.1]
- The three amendment rules were gazetted on 11 July 2025, tabled at LegCo on 16 July 2025, and took effect on 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, paras 1-2 and closing para]
- The HKMA finalised CRP-1 and revisions to nine other modules and a code of practice on 27 November 2025, all effective 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.1-2]
- CRP-1 is guidance; the binding classification rules sit in Part 12 of the Banking (Capital) Rules (BCR), which prevails if the two differ. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- Group 1 requires all four classification conditions: same rights and risks as the traditional asset (or an effective peg); legally enforceable rights and settlement finality; adequately controlled network risks; and regulated entities performing key functions. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.4.1, 2.5.1]
- Group 1a is tokenised traditional assets and Group 1b is stablecoins with an effective stabilisation mechanism; anything else is Group 2. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1-1.3.3]
- A Group 2 asset reaches Group 2a only if it meets three hedging criteria, including average market capitalisation of at least HKD 78 billion and 100 or more real price observations. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 3.1.1]
- Group 2b exposures take a 1,250% risk weight, which also covers their market and CVA risk. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, columns (c)-(e), p.215]; [S:5d845665ba83, para 4.3.2]
- Before acquiring a new type of cryptoasset, a bank must notify the HKMA and treat it as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees a better classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- Exposures held before 1 January 2026 must sit in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the bank's assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.2]
- If the HKMA disagrees with a bank's classification, it will override it. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.6]
- On permissionless chains, stablecoins licensed by the HKMA are deemed to meet the extra measures; other stablecoins need a comparable regime. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.6.3]
- The June 2026 letter says the approval condition for tokenised traditional assets on permissionless chains can also be met where a financial market regulator supervises the tokenisation business. This widens the route to Group 1. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- CA-G-1 section 8.7 says Group 1a banking-book exposures follow the underlying asset's rules, while Group 1b needs separate capital for the reference asset and the redeemer. [S:5d0c13e09312, paras 8.7.1-8.7.2]
- Group 2 exposure limit: a global or domestic systemically important bank (G-SIB or D-SIB) faces an add-on above 1% of Tier 1 capital and a harsher treatment above 2%. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(d)]; [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, rows 8-10, p.215]
- Under LM-1 Annex 3, only a Group 1a token of an asset that already qualifies as high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) can count as HQLA; a bank issuing a stablecoin redeemable within the LCR period applies a 100% outflow. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 paras 1, 7]
- Market risk: any cryptoasset exposure removes the de-minimis exemption, internal models cannot be used for Group 2 instruments, and Group 2a position risk is 100% of the net position. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80, paras 6.1.9, 6.2.8]
- CR-G-8 values crypto exposures under new Division 5A of the Banking (Exposure Limits) Rules; exposures with no counterparty default risk are ignored for large-exposure limits. [S:0cd3c1a74e5e, paras 2.8.8-2.8.9 and footnote 13]
- CR-L-5 treats a token carrying the economics of equity as share capital for the major-acquisitions consent rules. [S:13365a31e794, footnote 1]
- CA-G-5 says the HKMA may respond to crypto-related weaknesses with capital add-ons, provisions, limits or other measures. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Classify every cryptoasset exposure under BCR Part 12 and CRP-1, and keep assessing it on an ongoing basis. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 2.1.1]
- [ ] Move an asset to Group 2b at once if it stops meeting its conditions or criteria. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.3]
- [ ] As an RI, book loans secured only by VA collateral as clean loans for capital. [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep policies, staff and IT able to assess cryptoasset risk, and document the evidence for each classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]
- [ ] For stablecoins, keep a monitoring framework that checks the stabilisation mechanism works as intended. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.2.4]
- [ ] If the bank is a G-SIB or D-SIB, track the Group 2 exposure ratio against the 1% and 2% thresholds. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, rows 8-10, p.215]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Notify the HKMA before acquiring any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- [ ] Give the HKMA classification evidence on request. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] For Group 1 assets, check that every entity redeeming, transferring, storing or settling the asset is regulated or meets suitable risk standards. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The capital rules are law from 1 January 2026; CRP-1 is guidance, and the BCR wins if they differ. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 1.4.1]
- New cryptoasset types need HKMA notification before purchase. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]

**To business heads**
- Until the HKMA agrees a classification, a new cryptoasset sits in Group 2b at a 1,250% risk weight. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]; [S:5d845665ba83, para 4.3.2]
- HKMA-licensed stablecoins are deemed to meet the permissionless-chain measures, but must still pass conditions 1-4. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.6.3]

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong implemented the Basel standard on the Basel date, 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, closing para]
- The HKMA can override our classifications and add capital or limits if it sees weaknesses. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.6]; [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Any crypto exposure ends our market-risk de-minimis exemption. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80]
- A stablecoin we hold is non-HQLA with a 0% LCR inflow and an 85% NSFR required-funding factor. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 7]

## Common mix-ups

- "The June 2026 CRP-1 letter tightened the rules." It loosened para 2.6.4 by accepting supervised tokenisation activity. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- "Internal models are only barred for Group 2a." MR-1 bars them for all instruments referencing Group 2 cryptoassets. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, para 6.1.9]
- "The 1%/2% Group 2 limit applies to every bank." All locally incorporated banks calculate the ratio, but only G-SIBs and D-SIBs face the add-on. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(d)]; [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 11-12]
- "Legacy holdings keep their old treatment." They sit in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.2]
- "CBDCs are cryptoassets." They sit outside the standard and are generally treated like the central bank's fiat. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.2.3 and footnote 4]

## Read these first

1. **SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets** — HKMA, V.1 effective 1 Jan 2026. Read paras 1.1.4, 1.4, 2.1, 2.6 and 3.1.1. The classification engine behind every capital number. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251125-15-EN/CRP-1.pdf
2. **SPM CRP-1: update on cryptoassets classification conditions** — HKMA, 3 Jun 2026. Read p.1. Changes how para 2.6.4 is met. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260603-1-EN/20260603-1-EN.pdf
3. **Cryptoassets standard: SPM modules, code of practice, disclosure templates and returns** — HKMA, 27 Nov 2025. Read pp.1-4. Lists every module changed and the reporting transition. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251127-1-EN/20251127-1-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The April 2026 BCR proposals (for example, removing cryptoassets from "cash item" and new Group 2b derivative hedging rules) closed for comment on 1 June 2026; no final rules are in the corpus. [S:1e9b351e81e7, Items 19, 45]; [S:f6b5ade120fe, landing page]

- The corpus copies of the HKMA's December 2022 BCBS relay letter and the July/August 2025 gazettal letters are catalogue pages only.

title: Regulatory reporting and disclosure
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can say which HKMA returns and public (Pillar 3) disclosures now carry cryptoasset data, when the first filings fell due, and who could use the six-month transition.

## In 60 seconds

The Basel cryptoasset standard came with new reporting and disclosure duties, both effective 1 January 2026. On the reporting side, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) revised seven returns: liquidity (MA(BS)1E), the certificate of compliance (MA(BS)1F), capital adequacy (MA(BS)3, including a brand-new Part IIIf for crypto add-ons), market and CVA risk (MA(BS)3A), stable funding (MA(BS)26), leverage (MA(BS)27) and large exposures (MA(BS)28). Banks with no cryptoasset exposure on 1 January 2026 ('Transition AIs') could keep using the old templates for four of these returns until 30 June 2026. On the disclosure side, a new Part XII adds one narrative table (CAEA) and three templates (CAE1-CAE3) to the Pillar 3 package. A bank must publish these if it has cryptoasset exposures, with extra rows for material individual holdings. SPM module CA-D-1 explains how to apply the Banking (Disclosure) Rules (BDR).

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Banking (Disclosure) (Amendment) Rules 2025 | Government / LegCo | Gazetted 11 Jul 2025 | In force | All AIs | [S:277820235891, paras 1-2 and closing para] |

## Key facts

- The HKMA listed seven returns with new templates or instructions: MA(BS)1E, MA(BS)1F(a)/(b), MA(BS)3, MA(BS)3A, MA(BS)26, MA(BS)27 and MA(BS)28. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, 'Banking returns' list (a)-(g)]
- The HKMA said the final templates would not differ materially from the consultation versions, apart from textual, formatting and agreed changes. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- A Transition AI is one with no cryptoasset exposure on 1 January 2026; it could keep filing MA(BS)26, MA(BS)1E, MA(BS)3 and MA(BS)3A on the old templates until 30 June 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- Even Transition AIs had to use revised instructions for MA(BS)3 Part II and Part I paragraph 6 from 1 January 2026, for non-crypto changes. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, footnote 4]
- A bank with crypto exposure, or a Transition AI that later acquired some, could agree a temporary alternative arrangement with the HKMA for positions from 31 January to 30 June 2026 if its systems were not ready. [S:30b686db29f9, p.4]
- MA(BS)3 Part IIIf is new and must be completed by every Hong Kong-incorporated AI to work out additional risk-weighted amounts for cryptoassets. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 1]
- Part IIIf covers: an infrastructure add-on set by HKMA written notice; redemption-related credit risk for trading-book Group 1b and Group 2a stablecoins; each Group 2b position; and the Group 2 exposure ratio (all AIs) plus its add-on (G-SIBs and D-SIBs only). [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 3-12]
- The Part IIIf instructions carry a March 2026 version stamp, pointing to the quarter ended 31 March 2026 as the first capital-return period with the new crypto items. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, footer p.1]
- Parts IIIa and IIIb gain a separate Division A2 for cryptoasset exposures; Part IIIa also asks for the top five Group 1 cryptoassets by risk-weighted amount. [S:2195417bfd31, para 4 and Section C.3]; [S:df1dbac9c51a, para 4]
- Part IIIc (internal ratings-based approach) adds a memorandum form, IRB_CRYPTO, for banking-book Group 1 exposures. [S:4b2b2befa66f, Section C.6]
- MA(BS)1E is due 14 days after each month-end; category 1 banks report new memo items 1.7(a)-(b) on cryptoassets counted as HQLA and on tokenised customer claims. [S:f4e64fda4011, paras 5, 13.14]
- In MA(BS)1E, tokenised deposits can be reported like ordinary deposits but never get the 3% or 5% stable-deposit outflow rate. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]
- MA(BS)26 is quarterly, due within one month; category 1 banks add items 3(a)-(b) on tokenised claims and cryptoassets for the net stable funding ratio (NSFR). [S:767a346fbcaa, paras 4, 14]
- MA(BS)27 includes cryptoassets in the leverage exposure measure at their financial-reporting value. [S:3955600d53f0, para 6.5]
- MA(BS)28 is quarterly, due within one month; crypto exposures with no counterparty credit or default risk can be left out. [S:527c897d3eed, paras 4, 12]
- Pillar 3: the revised disclosure package applies to any reporting period ending after 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- Table CAEA is annual and covers crypto activities, risks, and how the bank assessed each Group 1 classification condition, using public information only. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA, p.210-211]
- Template CAE1 (exposures and risk-weighted amounts by Group) and CAE2 (accounting classification) are semi-annual for Hong Kong-incorporated banks with crypto exposures. [S:9e8d84c87168, Templates CAE1 p.212, CAE2 p.216]
- CAE1 needs extra rows for each material stablecoin or unbacked cryptoasset; for Group 2 an exposure is material when the Group 2 ratio is at least 0.3% and the single asset exceeds 5% of total Group 2 exposure. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214-215]
- CAE1's narrative must state the market value of cryptoassets the bank holds in custody for clients, split by type. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 accompanying narrative, p.212]
- CAE3 (liquidity) is semi-annual and fixed-format, for category 1 institutions with crypto exposures, whether incorporated locally or overseas. [S:9e8d84c87168, Template CAE3, p.218]; [S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, p.61-62]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] File the revised crypto items in MA(BS)1E, 3, 3A, 26, 27 and 28 on the stated schedules. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]; [S:f4e64fda4011, para 5]; [S:767a346fbcaa, para 4]; [S:527c897d3eed, para 4]
- [ ] Complete MA(BS)3 Part IIIf, including the Group 2 exposure ratio. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 1, 11]
- [ ] Publish Table CAEA and Templates CAE1-CAE3 as they apply to the bank. [S:e10295e5fe20, para 12.2.4 and Annex A, p.61-62]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Use daily mean values over the period for Group 2a and 2b rows in CAE1. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (i), p.213]
- [ ] Run the 0.3% / 5% materiality test at each period end to decide which Group 2 assets need their own CAE1 row. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214-215]
- [ ] Follow the HKMA explanatory notes for each template, not just the BDR text. [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] If systems are not ready for the revised returns, agree a temporary arrangement with the HKMA. [S:30b686db29f9, p.4]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] For each Group 1 asset, keep the public evidence used to assess the four classification conditions, since CAEA asks for it. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA point (f), p.211]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Crypto reporting started on 1 January 2026; the no-exposure transition window ended on 30 June 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- CA-D-1 is interpretive only; the BDR prevails if they conflict. [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]

**To business heads**
- The first crypto holding ends any Transition AI easement: the bank must move to the new templates. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3-4]
- Client custody holdings are disclosed publicly by market value and type. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 accompanying narrative, p.212]

**To the CEO**
- Our public Pillar 3 report now has a crypto section: an annual narrative plus semi-annual numbers. [S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, p.61-62]
- Seven HKMA returns changed at once for the cryptoasset standard. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Every local bank reports its Group 2 exposure ratio; only G-SIBs and D-SIBs report the add-on. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 11-12]
- Tokenised deposits never get stable-deposit outflow rates in the liquidity return. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]

## Common mix-ups

- "No crypto, no reporting change." Transition AIs still had to apply revised MA(BS)3 instructions for non-crypto items from 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, footnote 4]
- "The transition covered all seven returns." It covered only four: MA(BS)26, 1E, 3 and 3A. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- "Part IIIf redemption risk is a banking-book item." The source text places Group 1b redemption risk in the trading book (BCR section 376); some summaries say otherwise. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 5]; [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(a)]
- "Overseas-incorporated banks disclose nothing." CAEA (liquidity-risk activities) and CAE3 (if category 1) apply to them too. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA scope, p.210; CAE3 scope, p.218]
- "Every stablecoin needs its own row." Group 2 rows follow the 0.3% / 5% test; Group 1b follows general BDR materiality. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214-215]

title: AML/CFT for digital assets at a bank
md:
For the Head of Compliance (digital assets) at a Hong Kong bank: after this module you can say which anti-money-laundering (AML) texts actually bind the bank for virtual-asset (VA) business, where the VA-specific hooks sit, and which SFC and FATF material is context or counterparty expectation only.

## In 60 seconds

The bank's AML rulebook for digital assets is the HKMA's AML/CFT Guideline for Authorized Institutions (AIs), revised in May 2023 and effective 1 June 2023 — not the SFC's guideline. Its VA content is thin: a HK$8,000 trigger for customer due diligence (CDD) on walk-in VA transfers, a footnote pointing to the statutory travel rule at Schedule 2, section 13A of the AML Ordinance (AMLO), five-year record keeping, and correspondent-style checks on overseas virtual asset service providers (VASPs). The HKMA's January 2022 circular adds the expectations that matter day to day: watch customers' flows to and from VA platforms, risk-assess each VASP customer, and talk to the HKMA before launching any VA product. The SFC's AML guideline (with its Chapter 12 on VAs) binds licensed corporations and licensed platforms; it reaches the bank only for its SFC-registered (RI) business, as something to 'have regard to', and when the RI handles client VA deposits or withdrawals. Recent SFC circulars and FATF reports describe the live typologies — scam money layered through brokers and platforms, eDDA abuse, stablecoins moving through unhosted wallets.

## Key facts

- The HKMA Guideline is the AML rulebook for every AI, including AIs registered with the SFC; in it both 'must' and 'should' are mandatory. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.3, 1.6]
- Walk-in VA transfers: an AI should complete CDD before carrying out an occasional VA transfer worth HK$8,000 or more, including linked smaller transfers. [S:7bfdad704174, para 4.2.1(b)(iii), 4.2.4]
- For VA transfers the Guideline only points to AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A (footnote 15); its wire-transfer chapter does not mention VAs, so the statute is the operative travel-rule text for the bank. [S:7bfdad704174, para 4.2.1 fn 15; Chapter 10]
- The HKMA has stated that the AMLO does not stop AIs carrying out VA transfers for customers if section 13A conditions are met. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- Records for occasional VA transfers at or above HK$8,000 should be kept at least five years after the transaction; relationship records five years after the relationship ends. [S:7bfdad704174, para 8.4]
- If the bank gives correspondent-like services to FIs or VASPs located outside Hong Kong, it should apply the cross-border correspondent measures in paras 11.6 and 11.13; AMLO-defined FIs are carved out. [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23, fn 78–79]
- For an overseas VASP customer the bank should establish whether the account is for the VASP's own use or for serving its clients, and may require separate accounts for the two. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.24–11.25]
- RIs, and AIs that are associated entities of SFC licensees, must have regard to the SFC's AML Guideline, including Chapter 12 on VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 1 to para 1.3; S:8934af8cc884, para 4.16.1]
- The HKMA expects AIs to watch for customers who make frequent transfers to or from VA platforms, understand those flows, and file suspicious transaction reports (STRs) where grounds exist. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3–4]
- For VASP customers, due diligence should be risk-differentiated: understand the business model, check licensing and whether overseas rules are comparable, and assess the VASP's own AML controls. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- An AI planning any VA activity should discuss it with the HKMA and get feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, 'AIs' VA-related proposals', p.5]
- Intermediaries (LCs and RIs) that let clients deposit or withdraw VAs should comply with SFC Chapter 12 for those movements, and the same applies to VA-funded fund subscriptions and redemptions. [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b); S:b79266f3da51, para 7(c)]
- SFC Chapter 12 requires the ordering firm to obtain and pass on originator and recipient details for VA transfers of HK$8,000 or more; for unhosted wallets it should collect similar details from its own customer. [S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.5, 12.14.2]
- Licensed stablecoin issuers run a full travel rule at HK$8,000 and, unless their controls are proven effective, are expected to verify the identity of every holder. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 6.5–6.6, 5.11]
- The SFC reports scam proceeds being layered through licensed firms, some converted to VAs and withdrawn to unhosted wallets. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 8]
- Police figures given to LegCo: VA-related crime cases rose from 1,397 (2021) to 2,336 (2022) and 3,415 (2023), with sums involved of HK$824m, HK$1,704m and HK$4,398m. [S:4bd22ccf481d, reply (1)–(2)]
- An HKMA speaker noted that Hong Kong logged over 44,000 deception cases in 2024, a rise of close to 12% from the year before. [S:165d354a94bc, remarks on fraud and scams]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Complete CDD before any walk-in VA transfer of HK$8,000 or more, and aggregate linked transfers. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1(b)(iii), 4.2.4–4.2.5]
- Meet AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A for VA transfers the bank carries out. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15; S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- Run an ML/TF risk assessment and put mitigants in place before launching any VA-related product, service or new technology. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10–2.11; S:2b4123d71a07, p.2]
- Keep VA transfer and relationship records for the periods in para 8.4. [S:7bfdad704174, para 8.4]

**Controls & monitoring**
- Monitor customers' VA-platform flows and look into their nature. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3–4]
- Keep transaction-monitoring thresholds documented, reviewed and independently validated. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 5.4–5.8]
- In the RI business, apply SFC Chapter 12 when handling client VA deposits and withdrawals. [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss any planned VA activity with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- For the RI: notify the SFC and HKMA before starting or changing VA dealing, advisory or asset-management activity. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- File STRs with the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) where suspicion remains. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 5.10–5.14]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- For overseas VASPs receiving correspondent-like services: understand the business, check reputation and supervision, assess AML controls, get senior management approval. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.6, 11.23]
- Confirm with a VASP customer that its operations do not breach applicable laws in Hong Kong or elsewhere. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- Expect licensed platforms and brokers to register client bank accounts and whitelist wallet addresses — useful when reconciling flows with them. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 20]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Our governing AML text for VAs is the HKMA AI Guideline; SFC Chapter 12 applies only to our RI business and to VA deposits or withdrawals it handles. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 1; S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]
- The travel rule for our own VA transfers comes from AMLO Schedule 2 s.13A, not the wire-transfer chapter. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15]

**To business heads**
- Any VA product needs a documented ML/TF risk assessment and an HKMA conversation before launch. [S:7bfdad704174, para 2.11; S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- Banking an overseas exchange means correspondent-style due diligence and senior management sign-off. [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA does not bar us from VA transfers if statutory conditions are met; the bar is controls, not permission. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- Official data show VA crime sums rising to HK$4.4bn in 2023; fraud is the main threat to watch. [S:4bd22ccf481d, reply (1)–(2)]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Watch named red flags: rapid deposit-and-withdraw with no trading, and eDDA setups followed by new wallet whitelisting. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 7; S:cfc4a0d9f1be, para 11]
- FATF issued a focused report covering stablecoins and unhosted wallets in March 2026. [S:00c9fbd119bf, p.3]

## Common mix-ups

- 'SFC Chapter 12 binds the bank.' It binds LCs and licensed VASPs; the HKMA confirmed banks stay on its own Guideline, with RIs only having regard to the SFC text. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.2; S:08a762f7233e, para 12.1.2]
- 'Chapter 10 of the HKMA Guideline is our crypto travel rule.' Chapter 10 covers money wire transfers; the VA hook is footnote 15 to s.13A. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15, Chapter 10]
- 'All VASP customers need correspondent-banking measures.' Para 11.23 targets VASPs located outside Hong Kong; others get normal risk-based CDD. [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23]
- 'VASPs are automatically high-risk.' The HKMA asks banks to differentiate individual VASPs' risks; there is no single approach. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- 'The 2026 custody annex removed AML duties.' The 2024 annex had its own AML paragraph and the 2026 text does not, but the AML Guideline still applies in full. [S:86e064b2a8d0, para 23; S:ce05e67bcdce, sections (A)–(H)]

## Read these first

1. **Guideline on AML/CFT (For Authorized Institutions), revised May 2023** — HKMA, 25 May 2023. Read fn 1 (p.3), paras 2.10–2.11, 4.2.1–4.2.5 with fn 14–15, 8.4, 11.6–11.25. Why: the bank's binding text. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20230525-4-EN/AML-2.pdf
2. **Regulatory approaches to AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs** — HKMA, 28 Jan 2022. Read pp.3–5. Why: the HKMA's day-to-day expectations on VA flows, VASP customers and pre-launch dialogue. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20220128-1-EN
3. **AML/CFT Guideline for LCs and SFC-licensed VASPs, Chapter 12** — SFC, 1 Jun 2023. Read 12.1, 12.11, 12.13–12.14. Why: what the RI business must have regard to, and what counterparties must do. https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/assets/components/codes/files-current/web/guidelines/guideline-on-anti-money-laundering-and-counter-financing-of-terrorism-for-licensed-corporations/AML-Guideline-for-LCs-and-SFC-licensed-VASPs_Eng_1-Jun-2023.pdf

## Open items

- The HKMA circular of 27 April 2023 on VA transfers (cited in the 2023 consultation conclusions) is not in the corpus; its content is unverified here. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- The text of AMLO Schedule 2 s.13A is not in the corpus, so its detailed data fields are not restated here.
- The HKMA said in 2025 it was drafting supplementary AML guidance for other digital-asset activities; no final version appears in the corpus. [S:0d6e6d0253ff, para 4.1]
- No official VA-crime statistics after 2023 were found; the FATF stablecoins/unhosted-wallets report itself is not in the corpus.
- The SFC eDDA and layering circulars bind LCs and VASPs; there is no matching HKMA circular for banks as payer banks in the corpus.

## Related modules

B-series (HKMA supervision of VA activity), C-series (RI conduct and custody), D4, D5, E1, E3.

title: Cyber, fraud and technology risk
md:
For the Head of Compliance (digital assets) at a Hong Kong bank: after this module you can separate the technology-risk rules that bind the bank (HKMA) from the SFC rules that bind its platform and broker counterparties, name the dated SFC deadlines, and describe the scam patterns regulators have flagged.

## In 60 seconds

For a bank, the technology-risk texts for digital assets are HKMA ones: the April 2024 list of risk considerations for distributed ledger technology (DLT) and the custody standards, updated in May 2026 with detailed wallet and key-management controls. The SFC has built a parallel, more prescriptive set for licensed virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) and brokers: the August 2025 custody circular after overseas hacks, a January 2025 inspection report, a June 2026 circular on AI-enabled cyberattacks, and a July 2026 mandate to replace SMS and email one-time passwords (OTPs) with phishing-resistant login by 8 July 2027. Those SFC circulars do not bind the bank as such, but they describe what the bank's VATP and broker counterparties must now have, and the HKMA's 2026 custody update mirrors many of them. On fraud, the HKMA has repeatedly warned about crypto firms calling themselves 'banks', fake tokens trading on licensed stablecoin issuers' names, and false claims of links to HKMA pilots.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Risk management considerations for the use of DLT | HKMA | 16 Apr 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:1884530ff235, Annex] |
| Updated custody expected standards (key management, wallet controls) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and local AIs' subsidiaries | [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11] |
| Findings from inspections of deemed-licensed VATPs (25EC3) | SFC | 16 Jan 2025 | In force | VATPs | [S:0c93d9a066e6, Appendix 1] |
| Cybersecurity webinar materials (25EC11) | SFC | 20 Feb 2025 | Superseded | LCs, VASPs | [S:0fcb48929954, p.1] |
| Custody of virtual assets (25EC44) | SFC | 15 Aug 2025 | In force | VATPs | [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7] |
| AI-enabled cyberattacks (26EC32) | SFC | 2 Jun 2026 | In force | LCs, VASPs, associated entities | [S:a4929c8f9f3e, p.1] |
| Phishing-resistant authentication and surveillance (26EC35) | SFC | 9 Jul 2026 | Issued, effective 8 Jul 2027 (latest) | Internet brokers, licensed VASPs | [S:724f4d9f786e, para 21(c)] |
| Alert: crypto firms misusing 'bank' | HKMA | 15 Sep 2023; 15 Nov 2024 | In force | Public | [S:fcbcbb5d9d99; S:19c8611c621a] |
| Alert: tokens using licensed issuers' names | HKMA | 28 Apr 2026 | In force | Public | [S:275e7319a841, para 2] |

Note: the SFC's own record ranks 25EC11 as historical webinar material; 'Superseded' is the closest chip.

## Key facts

- The HKMA says an AI's board and senior management carry full responsibility for DLT adoption and its risks, and should update technology-risk, continuity and outsourcing policies for DLT. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
- The HKMA expects banks to justify their choice of DLT network type and generally avoid permissionless networks for highly critical functions unless compensating controls exist. [S:1884530ff235, Annex items 2, 5]
- Banks acting as custodian should apply more rigorous private-key procedures covering generation, storage, backup, access and cold storage. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 8]
- The May 2026 HKMA custody update adds system-enforced whitelists for cold-wallet transfers, no smart contracts in cold wallets on public chains, and blocks on 'blind signing'. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10, 11(c), 11(i)]
- Keys and seeds should be generated and held in tamper-resistant devices such as hardware security modules (HSMs), and generated, stored and backed up in Hong Kong. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(b)]
- At least 98% of client VAs held by a bank custodian should be in offline cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l), fn 8]
- Wallet code needs strict segregation of duties and least-privilege admin access — one of the few 'must' lines in the annex. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(f)]
- Custody monitoring should run 24/7 including holidays and track vendor, protocol and cryptographic dependencies. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–25]
- The SFC's August 2025 custody circular took immediate effect for VATPs and says weaknesses persist whatever custody technology is used. [S:562c0f8addce, p.2; 'Way forward', p.7]
- SFC inspections found keys held outside Hong Kong, a cold wallet using a multi-signature smart contract, weak encryption, and hot-wallet miscalculations against the 98/2 rule. [S:0c93d9a066e6, Appendix 2 paras 5–6, 17–22]
- The SFC's AI-cyberattack circular holds senior management, together with the Manager-in-Charge of IT, ultimately accountable, and asks firms to review patching, access, detection, supply chain and incident response. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, paras 3, 6–15]
- HKCERT recorded 15,877 cybersecurity incidents in Hong Kong for 2025, up from 12,536 the year before. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, fn 1]
- The SFC no longer treats SMS or email OTP as phishing-resistant; brokers and VASPs must adopt passkeys or robust device binding by 8 July 2027, and large internet brokers immediately. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)]
- If a firm lacks adequate controls to stop large-scale unauthorised transactions through client accounts following a hacking incident, the SFC will hold it accountable for clients' losses. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 25]
- The OTP requirement grew out of a February 2025 SFC circular that only encouraged firms to stop using OTPs. [S:4ce7d53d6956, Notes]
- Only AIs may use the word 'bank' or take deposits; using it without HKMA consent is an offence under the Banking Ordinance. [S:fcbcbb5d9d99, para 3, note 1]
- In April 2026 the HKMA warned that tokens with the tickers 'HKDAP' and 'HSBC' were not issued by the two licensed stablecoin issuers, neither of which had issued a regulated stablecoin. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2–3]
- The HKMA's first Quantum Preparedness Index score for the sector is 2.3 out of 10, against an objective of full readiness by 2030. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Keep board and senior management ownership of DLT risk and update technology-risk, continuity and outsourcing policies. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
- For custody: run a full risk assessment before launch, with board oversight before and after. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]
- Meet the key-management controls in para 11 (HSMs, Hong Kong keys, no smart contracts in cold wallets, anti-blind-signing, 98% cold). [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11]

**Controls & monitoring**
- Enforce cold-wallet whitelists by system and verify each transaction. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10]
- Run 24/7 security monitoring, and test all changes before deployment. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24]
- Build DLT-specific scenarios (attacks, key loss, forks) into continuity plans for critical functions. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 10]
- Secure the bank's and critical service providers' cyber fundamentals; frontier AI cyber risks should not be underestimated. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 10]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss VA activity with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- Where the bank's group has SFC-licensed entities: report material cyber incidents to the SFC promptly, and notify the case officer at once if the July 2027 authentication deadline cannot be met. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, para 18; S:724f4d9f786e, para 23]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Assess node operators' trustworthiness and diversity before relying on a DLT network. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 5]
- For custody delegates: independent code review, understanding of release processes, and periodic security and recovery testing. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15]
- When relying on a VATP, check it meets SFC custody standards (HSMs, air-gapped signing, 24/7 security operations centre). [S:562c0f8addce, Sections II–V]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The SFC OTP ban binds brokers and platforms, not the bank directly; our own standard is the HKMA custody annex. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 1; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11]
- The HKMA 2026 custody text now mirrors the SFC's 2025 wallet controls. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11; S:562c0f8addce, Section III]

**To business heads**
- Custody keys stay in Hong Kong in certified hardware; smart contracts are out for cold wallets. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(c)]
- Counterparty platforms must switch clients off SMS OTP login by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 21(c)]

**To the CEO**
- Accountability sits with the board and senior management, not the vendor or the technology choice. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
- Phishing made up 57% of reported incidents in 2025, per the SFC. [S:724f4d9f786e, fn 5]

**To Risk / CRO**
- The HKMA quantum readiness score is 2.3 of 10, with 2030 as the sector objective. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]
- Fake 'bank' branding and look-alike stablecoin tokens are live impersonation risks to our name and customers. [S:19c8611c621a, para 2; S:275e7319a841, para 2]

## Common mix-ups

- 'Multi-party computation or multi-signature makes custody safe.' The SFC says weaknesses persist regardless of the custody solution. [S:562c0f8addce, p.2]
- 'The 50%/100% compensation cover applies to bank custodians.' That is the SFC VATP rule (compensation for 50% of cold-wallet and 100% of hot-wallet losses under VATP Guidelines para 10.22); the 2026 HKMA annex instead makes the bank liable for losses it causes and requires adequate financial resources. [S:0c93d9a066e6, Appendix 1 para 33; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- 'OTP is fine as a second factor.' Not for SFC-licensed brokers and VASPs from July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 7]
- 'The HKMA DLT considerations are hard rules.' They are non-binding supervisory considerations, without deadlines. [S:1884530ff235, Annex]
- 'A licensed issuer's name on a token means it is regulated.' The HKMA warned this is false. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2–3]

## Read these first

1. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets by AIs** — HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 10–11, 14–15, 23–25. Why: the bank's own key and wallet control baseline. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
2. **Risk management considerations related to the use of DLT** — HKMA, 16 Apr 2024. Read all ten items. Why: how the HKMA reviews bank DLT projects. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20240416-2-EN/20240416-2-EN.pdf
3. **Circular 26EC35 on robust authentication and surveillance** — SFC, 9 Jul 2026. Read paras 5–13, 21–25. Why: the counterparty deadline and liability line. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC35

## Open items

- No HKMA circular on phishing-resistant authentication for banks is in the corpus; the 2026 Policy Address mentions the HKMA promoting 'iAM Smart' step-up authentication in banks, without a rule. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(i)]
- The SFC cybersecurity circular of 6 February 2025 is referred to but not itself in the corpus. [S:4ce7d53d6956, Notes]
- The HKMA custody annex's cross-referenced staking guidance and the SFC's November 2024 generative-AI circular are outside this module.

## Related modules

D3, D5, E1, E2, E3.

title: Tax and information reporting
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain what the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) bill would require, where it overlaps with the bank's existing Common Reporting Standard (CRS) duties, and what the government has said about tax concessions for digital-asset funds.

## In 60 seconds

CARF is an Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) standard for yearly exchange of crypto-asset tax data; Hong Kong committed to it in December 2024 and consulted in December 2025. The Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026 appeared in the Gazette on 22 May 2026 and is now before the Legislative Council (LegCo); the corpus shows no passage as of 25 September 2026. If passed, CARF duties start on 1 January 2027 and amended CRS duties on 1 January 2028. A business that carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers is a Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Provider (RCASP) and would have to register, run due diligence, report and keep records, with fines for failure. Banks already report under CRS, and the amended CRS pulls in crypto-linked assets and digital money products. Separately, the government said fund and family-office tax concessions would cover digital assets from year of assessment 2025/26.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

Acronyms: FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau; IRD = Inland Revenue Department; HKMA = Hong Kong Monetary Authority; SFC = Securities and Futures Commission.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commitment to implement CARF (first exchanges from 2028) | FSTB | 13 Dec 2024 | Stated target | Hong Kong government | [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4] |
| CARF and amended CRS consultation paper | FSTB + IRD | 9 Dec 2025 | Superseded | Proposed RCASPs; CRS financial institutions | [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6, PDF p.48-49] |
| Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026 | LegCo / FSTB / IRD | Gazetted 22 May 2026; First Reading 3 Jun 2026 | Bill before LegCo | HK RCASPs (Part 2); reporting financial institutions (Part 3) | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(2)-(4)]; [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2] |
| IRD CARF web guidance | IRD | Undated (reflects bill) | Bill before LegCo | RCASPs | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| Fund / family-owned investment holding vehicle (FIHV) tax concessions to cover digital assets | FSTB / Financial Secretary | 26 Jun 2025; 25 Feb 2026 | Stated target | Privately offered funds; FIHVs; single-family offices | [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]; [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98] |

## Key facts

- On 13 December 2024 the government told the OECD Global Forum it would implement CARF, aiming for local law by 2026 and first exchanges from 2028, on a reciprocal basis with partners that protect data. [S:ea81f92ea327, paras 1, 4]
- The December 2025 consultation paper proposed amending the Inland Revenue Ordinance (IRO, Cap. 112) for both CARF and the amended CRS; comments closed on 6 February 2026. [S:252a7f86684e, paras 4, 7]
- The consultation called CARF and the amended CRS finalised global standards and sought views only on local implementation choices. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 8, PDF p.4]
- The bill appeared in the Gazette on 22 May 2026 and was put to LegCo for First Reading on 3 June 2026. LegCo's notice for that sitting said the Second Reading debate would be adjourned. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]; [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2]
- If passed, Part 2 (CARF) commences on 1 January 2027 and Part 3 (amended CRS) on 1 January 2028; the rest starts on gazettal. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(2)-(4)]
- The bill defines an RCASP as anyone whose business carries out crypto exchange transactions on customers' behalf, whether by acting as the other side of the trade, by brokering it, or by running a trading venue. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M "reporting crypto-asset service provider"]
- An RCASP becomes a Hong Kong RCASP (HKRCASP) through Hong Kong tax residence, incorporation, management from Hong Kong, a regular place of business, or a Hong Kong branch that carries out relevant transactions. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
- The bill requires an HKRCASP to register with the Commissioner by 31 January of the year after it first meets a nexus test. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(1)-(2)]
- Three kinds of transaction are reportable: crypto-to-fiat exchanges, crypto-to-crypto exchanges, and transfers. Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and specified electronic money products are outside the relevant crypto-assets CARF covers. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Scope of crypto-assets covered' and 'Transactions subject to reporting']
- RCASPs must get tax-residence self-certifications from new customers. For existing users they have 12 months after the rules start. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
- Records must be kept for six years after the return's due date. The duty passes to former directors if the entity is dissolved. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Record keeping requirements']
- Failing to register, do due diligence or file a return without reasonable excuse is an offence with a level 3 fine. Using a service provider is not, on its own, a reasonable excuse. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(1)-(3)]
- Extra fines apply: $500 a day for continuing registration or return failures. A due-diligence breach can be fined at $1,000 per affected user or controlling person, if higher. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)]
- The bill also provides a financial penalty in place of prosecution, with written representations and appeal to the Board of Review. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Penalty provisions']; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.82E-82F]
- Under the amended CRS, CBDCs and specified electronic money products join the depository-account concept. Derivatives referencing crypto-assets become financial assets, and crypto-assets become eligible investments for investment entities. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.5]
- The consultation proposed that an entity that is both a CRS reporting financial institution (RFI) and an RCASP report crypto sale or redemption proceeds under both regimes, not once. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.14-4.17]
- Policy Statement 2.0 said the government would propose adding specified digital assets to the qualifying transactions for profits tax concessions of privately offered funds and FIHVs, effective from year of assessment 2025/26 if LegCo approves. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]
- The 2026-27 Budget said a bill to be introduced in the first half of 2026 would class digital assets as qualifying investments for these concessions, aiming at year of assessment 2025/26. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98]

## What your bank must do

These duties bind only once the bill passes and commences. The bill is not yet law.

**Obligations**
- [ ] Map whether any group entity, as a business, carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers, including as intermediary. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- [ ] Test each such entity against the Hong Kong nexus rules, including branches. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
- [ ] Plan registration by 31 January of the year after nexus is first met. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(2)]
- [ ] Plan for due diligence from 1 January 2027, including self-certifications for existing users within 12 months. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]; [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
- [ ] Prepare CRS systems for amended CRS due diligence from 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)]; [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.18]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep CARF due-diligence evidence and reporting records for six years after each return's due date. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Record keeping requirements']
- [ ] If CARF work is outsourced, keep oversight; outsourcing is not a defence. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]
- [ ] Plan test-file validation of CARF data before filing; the consultation set Q4 2027 for this. [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6 item (1)(c)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] CARF notices and returns go to the Inland Revenue Department (IRD), not the HKMA or SFC; watch for the IRD CARF Portal and data schema. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement']

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Where the bank partners with a VA trading platform or custodian, note that the counterparty may itself be an RCASP with its own reporting. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Individuals and entities subject to due diligence and reporting requirements']

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The CARF bill had its First Reading on 3 June 2026. If passed, CARF duties start on 1 January 2027 and amended CRS on 1 January 2028. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]
- Outsourcing CARF work to a vendor is not, in itself, a reasonable excuse for failing to register, do due diligence or report. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]

**To business heads**
- Any customer crypto exchange service, even as intermediary, can make the entity an RCASP. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- New crypto customers will need a tax-residence self-certification; existing ones within 12 months of start. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong committed to CARF in December 2024, with first data exchanges targeted from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4]
- The government linked CARF to Hong Kong's reputation as a financial centre. [S:ab980a841782, para 3]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Fines can scale: $500 a day for continuing failures, or $1,000 per affected user for due-diligence breaches. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)]
- The consultation proposed dual CARF and CRS reporting of crypto proceeds for entities in both regimes. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.17]

## Common mix-ups

- "CARF is already law." It is a bill before LegCo; the IRD says the dates apply subject to passage. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]
- "Register by September 2027." That was the consultation plan. The bill sets 31 January of the year after nexus is first met. [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6 item (1)(b)]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(2)]
- "Amended CRS starts in 2029." Duties start on 1 January 2028; 2029 is the first amended-CRS exchange. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.18]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)]
- "CARF covers CBDCs and e-money." Those are excluded from CARF but brought into the amended CRS. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 1.5, 4.3]
- "The HKMA or SFC supervises CARF." The IRD runs registration, returns and penalties. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal' and 'Penalty provisions']

## Read these first

1. **Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026** — LegCo / IRD, gazetted 22 May 2026. Read Clause 1 (commencement), ss.50M-50R (definitions, nexus, registration, due diligence, returns) and ss.80R, 82E-82F (offences, financial penalty). The operative text. https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/pdf/carf/Inland%20Revenue%20(Amendment)%20(Crypto-Asset%20Reporting%20Framework%20and%20Amended%20Common%20Reporting%20Standard)%20Bill%202026(eng).pdf
2. **IRD: Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework page** — IRD. Read the Overview, nexus, due diligence, registration and penalty sections. Plain-language summary kept in line with the bill. https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/tax/dta_carf.htm
3. **Implementation of CARF and Amendments in Relation to CRS (consultation paper)** — FSTB/IRD, 9 Dec 2025. Read paras 4.3-4.18 (amended CRS and dual reporting) and Chapter 6 (timeline). Best source on the CRS overlap for banks. https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/government/publication/consultation/docs/2026/crypto-framework.pdf

## Open items

- Passage of the CARF bill is not recorded in the corpus as of 25 September 2026. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2]
- The consultation also proposed mandatory CRS registration for all RFIs from January 2027 and heavier CRS penalties. The bill's list of provisions in the corpus shows no RFI registration clause. Whether that proposal moved to other legislation is not stated. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 5.1-5.2, Chapter 6 item (2)(a)]
- Whether the final bill keeps the proposed dual-reporting default is not stated on the IRD page.
- The IRD has not yet published the lists of reportable and partner jurisdictions, the portal or the data schema. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Lists of reportable jurisdictions' and 'Reporting portal']
- Fund/FIHV concessions: the 2026 Policy Address says a bill easing taxes on fund vehicles, single-family offices and carried-interest earners has already passed. The corpus has no bill text confirming how digital assets are treated in the enacted version. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 40]
- The corpus does not say whether tokenised deposits count as specified electronic money products for CRS.

title: What's coming: the pipeline
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can list what is still coming in Hong Kong digital assets, say how far along each item is, and quote only the targets the government and regulators have stated.

## In 60 seconds

Four new licensing regimes for virtual assets (VAs) are coming: dealing, custody, advisory and management. All four have consultation conclusions, and the government says one bill will go to the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2026. The earlier plan for an over-the-counter (OTC) licence run by Customs was folded into the wider dealing regime. On the market side, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has opened perpetual contracts for professional investors, secondary trading of tokenised funds, and licensed stablecoins on trading platforms. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) targets 24/7 settlement and central bank money settlement in EnsembleTX, tokenised Exchange Fund Bills tests and a CMU OmniClear digital-asset platform by around end-2026. Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) tax duties start in 2027 if the bill passes, and Customs plans digital-asset analytics systems by 2029.

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026. Dates are those stated in the source; targets are the government's or regulator's own words, not forecasts.

Acronyms in this table: FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau; VATP = VA trading platform; LC = SFC-licensed corporation; RI = registered institution (a bank registered with the SFC); HKEX = Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing; CMU = Central Moneymarkets Unit; RCASP = Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Provider; CRS = Common Reporting Standard; IRD = Inland Revenue Department; FATF = Financial Action Task Force; VASP = VA service provider; DeFi = decentralised finance; AML = anti-money laundering.

## Key facts

- The February 2024 OTC proposal would have created a Customs-run licence for VA-for-cash trading, with banks exempt. [S:efcdb0ae3849, paras 2.6, 2.23]
- The June 2025 dealing paper widened that plan. It now covers brokerage, block trading and custody-linked dealing, after the consultation found more varied business models. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.8-1.9]
- For dealing and custody, the SFC will license and set standards; the HKMA is frontline regulator of banks and of stored value facilities. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]
- The December 2025 conclusions align VA dealing with Type 1 (dealing in securities). VA dealers must use SFC-regulated VA custodians for client VAs. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 3-5, 26]
- No deeming or grandfathering applies at commencement. Firms already vetted by the SFC or HKMA get an expedited track. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]
- Commencement dates are not set. The government and SFC will consider how long the market needs to adjust. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- VA advisory will mirror Type 4 and VA management Type 9. Only banks may register, rather than be licensed, for these two services. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 2]; [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10]
- VA management has no de minimis threshold. Any discretionary VA exposure needs a licence or registration. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 32]
- In June 2026 the government said the bill for all four regimes, covering stablecoins among other VAs, would go to LegCo later that year. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- Perpetual contracts on VATPs are for professional investors only. Margin collateral is limited to fiat or HKMA-regulated stablecoins or tokenised deposits. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets'; 'Margin arrangements']
- The SFC's tokenised-fund trading framework will start with tokenised money market funds, and the SFC plans a review before widening it. [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 7]
- For Relevant Stablecoins, VATPs need not apply the retail liquidity and index tests, but must disclose stabilisation and redemption details. [S:19d52ade6849, paras 4-5]
- EnsembleTX settles interbank tokenised deposits through HKD RTGS (real-time gross settlement) at first, with a stated path to 24/7 tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]
- The 2026 Policy Address targets tokenised Exchange Fund Bills tests by year-end, covering more than $1.3 trillion of bills. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- The SFC plans to run a digital-asset custody surveillance system from H2 2026 and switch on CrypTech surveillance in 2027. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)]
- Customs plans to launch the Digital Asset Transaction Analytics System (DATAS) and Anti-Money Laundering Analytics System (AMLAS) by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Part II item 209]
- The FATF approved a seventh targeted update on VA/VASP standards and a DeFi report at its June 2026 Plenary, to be published later. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Inventory current and planned VA dealing, custody, advisory and management activity against the four coming regimes. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 4]
- [ ] Treat commencement as a hard stop: no deeming arrangement is planned. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]
- [ ] Do not actively market VA advisory or management services to the Hong Kong public without a licence or registration once the regime applies. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 70]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Track the SFC's stated custody surveillance system (H2 2026) for impact on custody counterparties. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)]
- [ ] Track CARF commencement dates for any group entity that may be an RCASP. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Start pre-application talks with the SFC, or the HKMA as applicable, early for the dealing regime. [S:6186c01c6649, para 33]
- [ ] Existing and would-be VA advisers and managers are urged to talk to the SFC early. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 6]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Under the dealing regime, check that VA custodians used for client assets are SFC-regulated. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]
- [ ] Check that a stablecoin offered on a VATP is a Relevant Stablecoin from an HKMA-licensed issuer. [S:19d52ade6849, para 2]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- All four VA intermediary regimes have conclusions; one bill is targeted for 2026, with no grandfathering. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]; [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]
- Banks register with the SFC for these regimes; the HKMA stays frontline regulator. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]

**To business heads**
- VA management has no minimum threshold; any discretionary VA exposure needs a licence or registration. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 32]
- VATP perpetuals accept HKMA-regulated tokenised deposits as margin collateral. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Margin arrangements']

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA targets EnsembleTX central bank money settlement and 24/7 operation by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- CMU OmniClear is to launch a digital asset platform in 2026 for digital bond issuance and settlement. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Customs aims to have digital-asset transaction analytics (DATAS) running by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Part II item 209]
- The FATF's next VA/VASP update and a DeFi risk report are approved but not yet published. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]

## Common mix-ups

- "The Customs OTC licence is still coming." The 2025 dealing proposal revised and replaced that plan under SFC licensing. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.9-1.10]
- "Conclusions mean the regimes are law." A bill is still needed; commencement dates are not set. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- "Retail clients can trade VATP perpetuals." Only professional investors can. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets']
- "VA managers can use any custodian, like dealers." The rules differ: dealers must use SFC-regulated custodians, while private VA fund managers may appoint qualified custodians globally. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 56-57]
- "Policy Address items are commitments with legal force." They are stated targets, delivered later through separate instruments. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49-51]

## Read these first

1. **Consultation Conclusions on VA dealing and further consultation on VA advisory/management** — FSTB + SFC, 24 Dec 2025. Read paras 3-5, 26, 29-36 and footnotes 9-10. Core design, custody rule, transition and bank registration. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/consultation/doc?refNo=25CP12
2. **Consultation Conclusions: VA advisory and VA management** — FSTB + SFC, 26 May 2026. Read paras 6-12, 32, 56-57 and 62-70. Scope, no de minimis, custody choice and commencement. https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/VASPVAMSP_consultation_conclusion_e.pdf
3. **The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address** — HKSAR Government, 16 Sep 2026. Read paras 35-36, 49-51 and 99, and Part II item 209. The latest official list of stated targets. https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

## Open items

- No bill text for the four VA regimes is in the corpus as of 25 September 2026.
- Commencement dates for the VA regimes are not set. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- The custody technology standards (key management, storage ratios) were left for a separate consultation, which is not in the corpus. [S:ddc173e5aaa2, para 2.38]
- The CARF bill's passage is not recorded in the corpus. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2]
- The FATF seventh targeted update and DeFi report were not yet published as of the 14 July 2026 SFC circular. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]

title: Wholesale money, CBDC and cross-border projects
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): after this module you can explain the HKMA's central bank digital currency (CBDC) work, from e-HKD to mBridge and Ensemble, and say what compliance role the published designs give to banks.

## In 60 seconds

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has studied a digital Hong Kong dollar (e-HKD) since 2017, starting with wholesale (bank-to-bank) money. It consulted twice on a retail e-HKD in 2021-2022 and ran two industry pilot phases in 2023-2025. In October 2025 it decided wholesale uses come first, and it has not decided whether or when to launch a retail e-HKD. Its cross-border work grew from Project Inthanon-LionRock with the Bank of Thailand (BoT) into mBridge, a multi-CBDC platform that reached minimum viable product (MVP) stage in June 2024. Project Ensemble now links tokenised deposits and wholesale central bank money at home, with tie-ups in France, Thailand, Brazil and Shanghai. In every published design, banks keep the customer-facing compliance work: know-your-customer (KYC), anti-money laundering (AML) and sanctions checks.

As of 25 Sep 2026.
